title: The Benyuan Dharma Gate Is an Outer Path Attached to Buddhism
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

inline.s: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

A: The Benyuan Dharma Gate is, of course, an outer path attached to Buddhism. What is meant by an outer path attached to Buddhism is one that adheres to Buddhism while distorting and tampering with its doctrine.

It exploits such weaknesses of human nature among the faithful as shrinking from difficulty, taking easy shortcuts, and clinging to worldly pleasures, in order to fool the faithful and cheat them of fame and gain
, and even to attain some political aim
The Benyuan Dharma Gate wholly fits this definition, so it is a genuine, out-and-out outer path attached to Buddhism.
An ordinary outer path attached to Buddhism raises the banner of the Dharma,
fools the faithful
in order to cheat them of fame and wealth, and even to attain some political aim.
But the Benyuan Dharma Gate goes far beyond this:
it seeks to destroy the true Dharma of the Buddha from its very root.
Therefore, besides having a systematic false teaching that distorts and tampers with Buddhist doctrine, it also incites the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil so as to wreck the sangha.
And through the so-called
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
(see
“Appendix Five: The Triple Abolition and Establishment of the Benyuan Dharma Gate”
it slaughters those who differ from it in order to root out the true Dharma.
This is where the enormous harmfulness of the Benyuan Dharma Gate lies!

[Incite the breaking of precepts and doing evil to wreck the sangha] The Benyuan Dharma Gate holds that doing evil and committing crimes are all of no account, and that monks may take wives and eat meat. Its doctrinal canon, The Shinshu Doctrine, says:
“Though the offense of an ordinary person is great, compared with the power of the vow it is but a single grain in the vast ocean

(though the offense of an ordinary person is great, compared with the power of Amitābha Buddha’s vow it is like a single grain of millet compared with the great ocean — utterly insignificant. For the refutation of this fallacy, see
Appendix Nine:
Refuting “Recitation of the Name Surely Brings Rebirth” and “the Evil Person Is the True Capacity”
, so no matter whether a
(monk)
eats meat or keeps a wife.”

They loudly proclaim: no need for practice, no need to keep the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind; even doing evil for a whole life is of no account, because the evil person is the true capacity whom Amitābha Buddha saves. For example, Master Huijing, in The Essence of Master Shandao, says: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to manifest Amitābha’s original vow: the evil person is the true capacity.” And Master Xinyuan, Master Huijing’s disciple who took refuge in him, in The Salvation of Amitābha Is the Evil Person as the True Capacity, says: “Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha’s salvation — with what kind of sentient being as its true capacity? The evil person as the true capacity.”

According to the Benyuan Dharma Gate’s topsy-turvy teaching, its incitement to break precepts and do evil, and its scheme to slaughter those who differ, while it abolishes the whole Path of Sagely Practice
(every method of practice other than the Pure Land Dharma Gate)

, it will also slander the earnest, single-minded Buddha-recitation that accords with the teaching as “self-power recitation” and abolish it. At that point the Buddhist fold becomes a single unified world for those who neither earnestly and single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name, nor keep the precepts, nor cultivate merit, nor purify their own minds, and who may even do evil for their whole lives. Monks who eat meat and keep wives no longer shave their heads, and even the monk’s robe is laid aside for fear of public scrutiny when they break precepts and do evil. In this way, the true sangha that is the model for gods and men no longer exists, and the masses, unable to obtain the genuine Dharma and finding no fruit in their practice, lose faith in the Dharma. What a scene this is!
(This scene already has precedent; see
The Practice of the Teaching of Master Hōnen
When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning!
[When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning] When the cart in front overturns, the cart behind must take warning from it.
Q: Why must the Benyuan Dharma Gate be criticized?
A: Because the deeds of the Benyuan Dharma Gate possess the three great characteristics of
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha
. First,
topsy-turvy teaching
, replacing the true Dharma with a false teaching

(they loudly boast that for rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss there is no “need to cut off evil and do good,” no “need to keep the precepts,” that “doing evil and committing crimes are of no account,” that “the evil person is the true capacity whom Amitābha Buddha saves,” that “recitation of the name surely brings rebirth,” that “the gate of the great vow,” and so on — see the several appendices and the further reading.)
. Second,
inciting the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil

, corrupting the fourfold assembly of home-leavers and householders, and in particular seeking to destroy the true sangha that is the model for gods and men, so as to extinguish the Buddha’s true Dharma
(see the several appendices)
The Buddha said:
“In the future the destruction of the true Dharma will not come from the assault of the demons and heretics, but precisely from the corruption and collapse of the sangha!”
(On the Sangha Jewel)
Third, the slaughter of those who differ and the monopoly of all under heaven
(see the section
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
in the appendix)
making the Buddhist fold a single unified world of false teachings and evil persons.
In this way, the Buddha’s true Dharma is destroyed.
And the retribution for destroying the Buddha’s true Dharma is most painful:
whether the propagators of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, or their followers, patrons, and supporters
(the karmic guilt of these latter three kinds of persons is that of being the tiger’s ghost helper)
all will fall into the Avici hell for long kalpas.
Therefore, whether for the sake of protecting the true Dharma or out of compassion, the Benyuan Dharma Gate must be criticized,
so that everyone comes to know the truth.
(Those who deliberately do evil certainly deserve their retribution; but those faithful who are fooled and mistakenly board a pirate ship, and in a confused way follow them to create karmic evil
(destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha)
and receive retribution
(falling into the Avici hell for long kalpas)
, are truly pitiable and hardly worth it. O vast and boundless heavens, what manner of men are these!)
In the Buddha Treasury Sutra

in the chapter on ancient times, the seventh, the Buddha, when speaking of the retribution of those who in the past destroyed the true Dharma of the Buddha and of their followers, patrons, and supporters, says:
These evil persons,
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha,

also bring great ruin and affliction upon many people. Moreover, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avici hell, lying on their backs for nine hundred trillion years, lying on their faces for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the left side
(lying on the left side)
for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the right side
(lying on the right side)
for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charring
(the same as ‘scorched’)

upon the hot iron. Dying there, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, experiencing all such suffering for the same number of years as above. Dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again in the great Avici hell.
Śāriputra,
for this reason, whether householders or home-leavers who draw near such a person
(the followers of these evil persons)
, and the good teachers
(good knowing companions, that is, the supporters of these evil persons)
and all the patrons
(the benefactors and patrons of these evil persons)
, in all six hundred forty trillion persons, together with these four teachers
(together with these four evil persons)
live and die together, and in the great hell undergo all manner of burning and boiling.
Thus, Śāriputra,
all the good-teacher households of such a person, all the patron households, disciples, teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number — are born in hell.

Śāriputra, you cannot know how many there are; only the Tathāgata can know. Those who with these evil persons fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one kalpa, remaining in hell until the conflagration of the great kalpa. Why? Śāriputra, to break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Tathāgatas is an offense very heavy, not light. When the great kalpa burns, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avici great hell and are reborn elsewhere, in the great hell. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in other regions, for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When the world comes into being again, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with the others whose offenses are not yet finished, at their death are reborn again in the great hell of this world.”

(Translation: These evil persons, destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha, also cause many who follow them to suffer great distress. Moreover, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avici hell, lying on their backs upon the hot iron for nine hundred trillion years, on their faces for nine hundred trillion years, on the left side for nine hundred trillion years, and on the right side for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charring in the Avici hell. After dying in the Avici hell, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, undergoing in each of these hells in turn the manifold suffering of lying on the back nine hundred trillion years, on the face nine hundred trillion years, on the left side nine hundred trillion years, and on the right side nine hundred trillion years. Finally, dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again into the great Avici hell to continue their suffering. Śāriputra, for this reason, all householders and home-leavers who draw near these four evil monks, and their close associates (good teachers), and their patrons (benefactors), in all six hundred forty trillion persons, live and die together with the four evil monks, fall together into hell, and undergo all manner of burning and boiling in the great hell. Thus, Śāriputra, all the supporters of these four evil monks, the households of all the patrons (benefactors), the disciples, the teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number — are born in hell. Śāriputra, you cannot know how many there are; only the Tathāgata can know. Those who with these four evil monks fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one great kalpa, remaining in hell until the conflagration of the kalpa. Why? Śāriputra, they break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas — an offense very heavy, not light. If at the end of a corrupt kalpa the conflagration burns, these four evil monks and the six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avici great hell and are reborn in great hells elsewhere. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in the great hells of other regions, for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When this world again comes into being, these four evil monks and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with the others whose offenses are not yet complete, at their death are reborn again into the great hell of this world.)
[Being the tiger’s ghost helper (
chang

)] To act as the tiger’s ghost helper. In old legend, a person eaten by a tiger becomes, after death, a ghost helper whose sole function is to lure people for the tiger to eat. [One kalpa] Here it refers to one great kalpa. A great kalpa contains the four intermediate kalpas of formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness. At the end of the kalpa of destruction, the fire, water, and wind calamities necessarily arise.

inline.s: Master Weixian

[Master Weixian] A native of Pengxi, Sichuan, he entered the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Academy at the age of fourteen and was highly esteemed by Master Taixu, his Buddhist learning being profound. In his youth he already had essays and treatises that made his name known throughout the Buddhist world. In the 1950s he was buffeted by political movements and imprisoned for twenty-six years, enduring great hardship. In prison he practiced diligently without cease and studied the Buddhist canon deeply. On his release in the 1980s he became the abbot of Chongqing Ciyun Temple and widely spread the good karmic conditions of the Dharma. With his profound learning he taught the Dharma and transmitted the precepts at monasteries at home and abroad, winning deep reverence throughout the Buddhist world. He served as chairman of the advisory committee of the Buddhist Association of China, president of the Chongqing Buddhist Association, and head of the Chongqing Buddhist Academy. He passed away at Tushan Temple in Nan’an District, Chongqing, at 4:50 a.m. on February 2, 2013, at the age of ninety-three.
[Note] This essay reveals that China’s Benyuan Dharma Gate, whether in doctrine or in funds, all derives from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate,
and is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate:
More and more evidence shows that the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money as its support,
and possessing channels and bases for
printing books and recording tapes,
and moreover possessing those who
preach and incite — monks, nuns, and laypersons and so on.
About two years ago (that is, 1997),
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate got in touch with temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be established, it could remit ten million yuan.
These
“Benyuan Dharma Gate” centers

established with funds from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate, because the name ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ is too notorious, now change to such brands as “relying on Master Shandao,” “promoting Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought,” “promoting Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma Gate,” and the “Shandao school,” and try as far as possible to conceal their connection with the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate. These people, harboring a crooked heart and practicing deceit, think that all can be deceived and that no one in the world is as clever as they
(that there is no one in the world cleverer than me)
, not realizing that evil retribution is behind, coming one after another.
Master Shandao instructed: “What has come is true, and what is sincere is real. To make clear that the practice and understanding accomplished in body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings,
must be done with a true and genuine mind.

One must not outwardly manifest the appearance of virtue and diligent effort while inwardly harboring falsehood — greed, hatred, perversity, deceit, all manner of cunning — an evil nature hard to change, a matter like venomous snakes and scorpions. Though one sets body, speech, and mind in motion, it is called the goodness of mixed poison, and also called the practice of falsehood, not real karmic action. If one settles the mind and so practices, then even if one toils body and mind, day and night through the twelve hours, rushing and pushing as though one’s head were on fire, it is all
(with ‘all’ meaning ‘altogether’)
called the goodness of mixed poison.
To wish to turn back from this mixed-poison practice and seek rebirth in that Buddha’s Pure Land is entirely impossible.
” (The Four-Volume Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra)

[It is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate] Master Jingkong’s Questions and Answers in Buddhist Study, answering the seventy-fourth session of fellow practitioners visiting Hong Kong, contains this: “Q:
A home-leaver has recently been expounding the Dharma in various places around China, and is in fact promoting a heresy — the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate.
Their method is this: if a monastery is willing to publicize the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū for them, they invest ten million renminbi at one stroke.
. Second,
if a Chinese layperson is willing to publicize the Jōdo Shinshū for them on the internet, they can supply a monthly salary and bonus.

. The concrete way of working is that the Chinese layperson comes forward to establish a forum, and they assign a person on a full-time basis each day to repost the posts of the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū on the various Buddhist Pure Land forums.

If this Chinese layperson is very rich in Buddhist knowledge, they can supply a monthly salary of ten thousand renminbi (note: the layperson’s monthly salary is ten thousand renminbi; if it is a Dharma master, what monthly salary do they supply?)

. The Japanese demand is that this seller of Buddhism should pretend to be a devoted disciple of the Founding Master Yinguang, Master Jingkong, or an esoteric master, mix with ordinary Buddhist friends on the internet, and make everyone admire their Buddhist foundation, and then lead ordinary Buddhist friends to accept the views of the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū. On the above matters I ask the Elder Master to instruct.”

[Honganji] Honganji is the head temple of the Honganji branch of the Jōdo Shinshū of Japanese Buddhism. [Jōdo Shinshū] Also called the Benyuan school, it permits monks to take wives and bear children, and propagates the Benyuan Dharma Gate of “recitation of the name surely brings rebirth, the evil person is the true capacity.”
Lately, from Buddhist publications and from actual contact, there is reflected
an undercurrent in China’s Buddhist community of “studying Japanese Buddhism and taking the Japanese Buddhist road.”
This undercurrent impacts from two sides. The first is to destroy the fundamental rule of China’s Han Buddhism requiring that monks must “wear the robe, be vegetarian, and remain celibate.”

A fair number of Japanese home-leavers take wives and bear children, drink alcohol and eat meat, wear Western suits, and disregard the precepts, which greatly pleases our own monks who do not keep the precepts.
The essay The Alarm Bell (published in Taizhou Buddhism,
, no.
, issue no.
) exposes: “It is now found that in key temples of City
W

four young and middle-aged home-leavers have already returned to lay life, and the head of the fairly famous ‘Kairu Sutra-Printing Society’ — the monk Kairu of Mount Jiuhua — again returned to lay life last year.” It is reported that
in some coastal cities of our country monks are in the temple by day, and at night return to their own private dwellings to live a family life,
and the social impact is extremely bad.
The second side of the impact is
the propagation of Japan’s “Benyuan Dharma Gate,”
which seeks to interfere with and destroy it in spirit and in the direction and path of Buddhist study and practice. The entry of Japanese Buddhism into China has been long-standing;
in the 1930s it served the war of aggression against China.

. The essay The Alarm Bell discloses that at that time in Wuhu, Anhui, “in the middle second street there was a Japanese Buddhist temple, with Japanese-style lanterns hung at the gate, bearing the red characters ‘Higashi Honganji,’ and within lived a Japanese monk and his whole family. The Japanese monk often held a leather drum and beat it as he walked along the streets. It is said that in all the other cities occupied by Japan there were such, and that they served with the army, exclusively performing rites for the dead Japanese.

At that time when Japan invaded China, they called it the ‘holy war’; to kill for the ‘holy war’ was without guilt, and the dead souls passed beyond to the Buddha-land. The glorious names of those who killed many Chinese and had merit could enter the ‘shrine.’ After the War of Resistance ended, the unpopular Japanese Buddhism vanished from mainland China.
Who would have thought that this specter has been resurrected by ‘a group of people
(namely Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others)
’ — is not that absurd?
The Shanghai layman Zheng Songying, in the essay Destroying the Heterodox and Revealing the Right, Eliminating the Three Harms published in Taizhou Buddhism, points out: “The Japanese
‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ has recently already been transmitted to China
, and though it seems a school of the Pure Land Dharma, it is entirely contrary to the Buddha’s Dharma, misleads sentient beings, and does great harm,
and is in fact a heretic within the teaching!

It advocates that so long as one hears the name of Amitābha Buddha and can bring forth faith, one has obtained the ‘identity card’ of the Land of Utmost Bliss, and is certain to be reborn there! No more reciting the Buddha’s name and practicing; no matter how one dies, and without the deathbed assistance of recitation, one is certain to be reborn!” “The ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ requires only a single ‘faith’ and no ‘practice’ at all, relying on other-power alone and not self-power — is this still Buddhism?” In fact, in the late Qing and early Republican era, the layman Yang Renshan, through the Japanese Buddhist scholar Nanjō Bun’yū, imported a great many Buddhist scriptures, and with regard to the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ he subjected it to criticism and rejection. (See the Clarification of the Teaching Compilation in the Continued Canon
the twelfth kind compiled by the layman Yang.) No master of the Pure Land school in China’s modern and contemporary period has ever advocated the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate.’
More and more evidence shows that
the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money as its support,
and possessing channels and bases for
printing books and recording tapes,
and moreover possessing those who
preach and incite — monks, nuns, and laypersons and so on.
. About two years ago,
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate got in touch with temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be established, it could remit ten million yuan.

. At that time they also had doubts about the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ claim that only a single ‘faith’ is needed and one may dispense with reciting the Buddha’s name and practicing. But they again thought of using this large fund to build a center and in the future still promote the pure and correct Pure Land school, and wrote to the elder layman Zheng Songying in Shanghai to ask his advice. The elder Zheng’s reply pointed out: “To do so is to set an improper motive-ground, and it should be firmly refused and not accepted.” Only then did they desist.
It is now established that the centers propagating the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ are very many, and those with frequent activity number several.
The essay The Alarm Bell says: “In the past two years, Taiwan’s
Japanese Jōdo Shinshū Benyuan Dharma Gate
has repeatedly mailed books, publicity materials, and so on to the various Buddhist institutions of Anhui, and some Buddhists have already come under its influence.”
There are two young and middle-aged home-leavers who call themselves of Mount Jiuhua, propagating Japanese Buddhism in various cities; one of them, eloquent, is called ‘Master Holy Su (
now renamed Master Jingzong, having run off to take refuge with Master Huijing of Taiwan, who advocates the Benyuan Dharma Gate
),’ and using people’s reverence for the sacred ground of Mount Jiuhua and respect for the monks of Mount Jiuhua, they find connections to help them arrange venues to preach,
pleasing the devout good believers of little experience and the home-leavers who do not keep the precepts.

During the Spring Festival this year, the two monks Holy Su and another, accompanied by a Taiwanese nun, came down from the mountain again to preach. From Xuancheng to Wuhu they gave one day’s preaching and one day’s discussion,
and afterward were called to account by the municipal Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference and the Religious Affairs Bureau.
, in the first half of the year, this undercurrent again penetrated deep into the southwest, and Chongqing Municipality was most heavily affected. Not only did the Cangtangyan

of Xuancheng, Anhui, and the “Ciyuan Group Bodhi Monastery Gift Center” of Dezhou, Shandong, send in bulk such books as the Amitābha Calling series, but in the summer they also sent a young monk to the Chongqing urban area, very secretively, without revealing the name of his original monastery or his Dharma name, lodging in the home of a layperson and organizing group after group of faithful to hear him advocate the “Benyuan Dharma Gate”; those deluded grew daily, until the lay practitioners who practiced the Pure Land Dharma Gate in Chongqing split into two factions. Some lay practitioners who upheld the Pure Land “two powers” (Buddha-power and self-power) Dharma Gate put many questions to this monk, but his replies were unclear, and he even said angrily: “You will fall into hell! Fall into hell! Fall into hell!”
Judging from the above circumstances, if this undercurrent is let to grow and spread, it will severely corrode, and even destroy, the whole of Buddhism.

(Original editor’s note: The Benyuan Dharma Gate distorts the three Pure Land sutras and one treatise, advocating that there is no need to recite sutras, keep the precepts, bring forth bodhicitta, or practice the bodhisattva’s six perfections and ten thousand practices — this altogether contravenes Buddhist doctrine and the Mahāyāna spirit that transcends the world while being in the world,
and is in reality
an outer path attached to Buddhism
, and it should arouse the high regard and resistance of the whole Buddhist community. It is also hoped that the relevant government departments pay attention

blocks.text: Appendix Two: Guard Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate on the Pure Land School

inline.s: [Original editor’s note]

The essay Guarding Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate on the Pure Land School, in the magazine Sound of the Dharma, the journal of the Buddhist Association of China, lists many false teachings of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, and finally warns that “if its theory is allowed to circulate in the Buddhist community, it will have a destructive influence on the abiding of the true Dharma.”

blocks.text: 1. A Brief Account of the Origin and Development of the Benyuan Dharma Gate

inline.s: The theory of the Benyuan Dharma Gate originated with the Japanese Master Hōnen, and reached its peak with his disciple Shinran.

As the essay in Sound of the Dharma says, “its basic theory single-mindedly emphasizes other-power, and is in many places at variance with the sutras and treatises.” Yang Renshan, the father of the restoration of Chinese Buddhism, in his Critique of the Selected Collection of Original Vow Recitation says: “I find that this collection is at variance with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,” and in his Critique of the Shinshu Doctrine says: “I find it is at variance with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,”
and he criticized their false teaching as “
concealing the mechanism of the destruction of the Dharma
Master Hōnen’s theory had already deviated from Master Shandao, and the Jōdo Shinshū (Benyuan Dharma Gate) established by his disciple Master Shinran ran even more directly counter to Master Shandao.
Master Shandao’s thought is “even the evil person is reborn, how much more the good person”; but with the Jōdo Shinshū it became the “evil person is the true capacity” of “
even the good person is reborn, how much more the evil person”!
The “even ten recitations” of the eighteenth vow is also construed by the Benyuan Dharma Gate as “so long as one deeply believes in Amitābha’s original vow (the eighteenth vow),
with a single recitation one is reborn in the reward land

, and immediately attains Buddhahood, transcending the nine grades. Therefore there is no need for many recitations; otherwise it is not trusting Amitābha’s original vow, and so recitation is only an act of gratitude!”
(One of the characteristics of the Benyuan Dharma Gate: topsy-turvy teaching.)

For this reason, even Master Hōnen himself rebuked Shinran as “an outer path attached to the Buddha’s Dharma, a confederate of the demon hosts, destroying and extinguishing the Buddha’s Dharma, an outer path beyond the outer paths,” and warned the multitude: “Be careful not to follow that false teaching.”
Yet up to the present day, these false teachings that even Hōnen rebuked
have been inherited by Master Huijing and others, who promote the Benyuan Dharma Gate under the banner of the “Shandao school.”
Master Huijing’s The Essence of Master Shandao says: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to manifest Amitābha’s original vow:
the evil person is the true capacity
The Benyuan Dharma Gate is that the evil person is the true capacity

, other-power faith and practice, rebirth in the reward land. That is, the most evil and lowest person, relying on the most excellent and highest Dharma, is born in the highest and most wonderful land.”
Note:

The Sutra Praised by the Buddha: The Pure Land, which our teacher Śākyamuni Buddha proclaimed with his own golden mouth, and which is praised and received by Amitābha Buddha in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, says:
“Sentient beings of little root of good are not those who can attain rebirth in the pure Buddhaland of the Land of Utmost Bliss of Amitāyus Buddha.
(Translation: sentient beings with little root of good (the good of the three karmic actions of body, speech, and mind) cannot attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. See
Annotation on the Sutra Praised by the Buddha: The Pure Land

Yet the Benyuan Dharma Gate loudly advocates the evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine, making Amitābha Buddha’s great vow into a protective umbrella for the evil person. Its slandering of the Buddha and destruction of the Dharma go this far!
In the Contemplation Sutra of Infinite Life, the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds is not one who is reborn merely by reciting the name,
but rather one who has accomplished the ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death and, extinguishing his offenses, is reborn
(see
Annotation on the Lowest Grade and Lowest Birth Section of the Contemplation Sutra
. Originally, the “lowest grade and lowest birth section” of the Contemplation Sutra is about the grade of the person thus reborn
(the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who, having accomplished the ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death and extinguished his offenses, is reborn)
, which is the lowest grade and lowest birth; but the Benyuan Dharma Gate deliberately omits
the key of “ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death”

, exaggerating it into the claim that all persons of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who merely recite the Buddha’s name once are reborn, and even advocating the so-called evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine
(that Amitābha Buddha’s salvation takes the evil person as its true capacity)

Moreover, even those in the sutra who are said to attain rebirth despite the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds did so because in past lives they deeply planted good roots and once sowed the seed of bodhi. Master Ouyi
says
“The sutra says that those who attain rebirth despite the ten evil deeds and five heinous offenses
must have planted the seed of bodhi in the past.
If there were no seed of bodhi, how could they meet a good friend? Even if they met a good friend who urged them on, how could they at once bring forth faith and vow and recite the great name?”
(The Lingfeng Collected Treatises, General Sermon at the Tianma Monastery of Shepu)
Master Ouyi also says:
“As for the ten recitations at the time of death,
one must have deeply planted roots of goodness

. If even now, when adverse or favorable conditions arise, one no longer has right mindfulness, how much less at the time of death? Moreover, when the suffering of death appears, one can rely only on a good friend's prompting; yet today, under clear skies and bright sun, one still cannot accept and practice the true maxims of a clear teacher and good friend!”
(Lingfeng Zonglun,
Preface to Cultivating Pure Land Repentance and the Life-Release Society)
(Translation

: To accomplish the ten recitations at the time of death, one must deeply plant roots of goodness. If today, the moment adverse or favorable conditions arise, one no longer has right mindfulness, how much less will one be able to keep right mindfulness at the time of death? Moreover, under clear skies and bright sun, in broad daylight, one still cannot accept and practice the true admonitions of a clear teacher and good friend, and yet one vainly hopes that when the suffering of death appears, one can, merely by relying on a good friend's reminders and instruction, accept and practice them?)

The doctrine of ‘evil persons as the true recipients’ is utterly mistaken. The basis for study and practice in the Pure Land school is the Three Pure Land Sutras; let us see what these three sutras say:
In the Buddha Speaks of Amitābha Buddha Sutra, the Buddha says:
Not with few roots of goodness and blessings
and causal conditions can one be born in that land
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
In the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, the Buddha says:
Those who wish to be born in that land
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
should cultivate the three blessings
: First, to support and serve one's parents, to serve and respect one's teachers, to be compassionate and refrain from killing,
to cultivate the ten wholesome deeds
; second, to receive and uphold the three refuges,
to observe all the precepts
, and not to violate the rules of deportment; third, to arouse the bodhi mind,
to deeply believe in cause and effect
, to read and recite the Mahāyāna scriptures, and to encourage others to practice. These three matters are called pure karma.”
In the Buddha Speaks of the Immeasurable Life Buddha Sutra, the Buddha used many passages to teach the observance of precepts and the ending of evil and practice of good. For example:
“You should resolve decisively,
straighten your body and rectify your conduct, and strive to do all that is good
Cultivate yourself and purify your body; wash away the defilements of the mind
In word and deed be loyal and trustworthy
, so that the outer and the inner correspond. A person can save himself, and in turn rescue others; with clear understanding form your aspirations,
and accumulate the roots of goodness
. Though for one lifetime you labor and suffer, in but a moment,
you will afterwards be born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where bliss has no limit
“You should think this over carefully,
keep far from all evils, choose what is good, and diligently practice it
You devas and humans of the present, and people of later ages, when you obtain the Buddha's words, should ponder them well; if you can therein
rectify your minds and correct your conduct
Each of you should consider this well, and mutually instruct and admonish one another,
to conform to the Buddha's scriptures and Dharma, and not transgress them
“The world being thus, the Buddha pities them all. By his awesome spiritual power he destroys all evils,
causing all to turn to goodness
. Cast away your thoughts,
uphold the scriptures and precepts

, receive and practice the way of Dharma without transgression or loss, and in the end attain the way of deliverance from the world, nirvāṇa.” “You devas and humans of the present, and people of later ages, when you obtain the Buddha's words, should ponder them well; if you can therein
rectify your minds and correct your conduct
When rulers do good
and lead and transform those below them, mutually commanding one another,
each keeping himself upright
Honor the sages and respect the good; be kind, compassionate, and universally loving
Do not dare to fail or betray the Buddha's teaching and instruction

. You should seek deliverance from the world, uproot the source of all the evils of birth and death, and depart from the path of the three evil destinies with their immeasurable sorrow, fear, and suffering. Hereupon you
should widely plant the roots of virtue
, bestow kindness and grant benefits,
do not violate the prohibitions of the Way

Practice patience and diligence, single-mindedness and wisdom. Mutually teach and transform one another; establish virtue and do good. Rectify your mind and your intent; keep the fast and the precepts pure.
Do not follow your own desires at will, fail the scriptures and precepts, and fall behind others.

Yet the Original Vow school turns its back on the Three Pure Land Sutras, using the doctrine of ‘evil persons as the true recipients’ to incite people to break the precepts and do evil, corrupting the fourfold assembly of monastics and laity, and in particular seeking to destroy the true Saṅgha that is a model for gods and humans. This is the destruction of the Buddha's true Dharma!
The Buddha says:
“The future destruction of the true Dharma will not come from the ruin wrought by heavenly māras and outside paths, but from the corruption and collapse of the Saṅgha!”
(On the Treasure of the Saṅgha)

Inverted teachings of the Original Vow school can be found everywhere. For example, in Master Jingzong's long lecture series, The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao, what he keeps saying over and over is that the ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ are the very core of Master Shandao's Pure Land thought. What are the facts? The facts are:
Master Shandao never spoke of a Gate of the Vast Vow at all; it was entirely fabricated by Master Hōnen
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)
Nor did Master Shandao ever say that reciting the name brings certain birth; on the contrary, Master Shandao said: continuous recitation brings birth
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
and
The Eighteenth Vow
for details)

. The ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ that they fabricated themselves, they then foisted upon Master Shandao, falsely claiming this to be Master Shandao's Pure Land thought and calling themselves the ‘Shandao lineage’. In fact, they distort and slander Master Shandao
(see
How Hōnen and Others Distorted and Slandered Master Shandao
for details)

Moreover, their patriarch Master Hōnen not only fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow, but also distorted the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception, which is praised and upheld by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
(see
Master Hōnen's Distortion of the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception
for details)
. Not only that, they also slander the patriarchs of the Pure Land school
(including Master Yongming, who was a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha)

as impure and lacking a lineage, vainly attempting to overturn the lineage of the thirteen patriarchs of Chinese Pure Land and replace them with Hōnen and Shinran. All of this is sheer fabrication, confounding black and white.
Master Xinyuan, a disciple who took refuge under Master Huijing, says: “
Amitābha's deliverance takes evil persons as its true recipients
. Once we understand the principle concerning evil persons,
let us now look at Amitābha Buddha's deliverance: what kind of beings does it take as its true recipients? Evil persons are the true recipients.
The Tannishō says: ‘For us who are fully endowed with afflictions, no practice whatsoever can free us from birth and death. Amitābha, in his compassion,

made his vow with the fundamental intent that evil persons might attain Buddhahood; therefore the evil person who entrusts himself to the power of another is precisely the true cause of birth in the Pure Land
.’ The Tannishō records what Master Shinran taught.
(Note: this shows that the Original Vow school in China has inherited Shinran's mantle!)

After Master Shinran passed away, his ordained disciple Master Yuien recorded it. After Master Shinran's passing, some practitioners of Original Vow recitation in the Buddhist world of that time misunderstood the principles Master Shinran had taught; therefore his ordained disciple Master Yuien wrote down what Shinran had taught, and this became the Tannishō, a work that has circulated very widely throughout the countries of the world. The Tannishō says: for us who are fully endowed with afflictions, no practice whatsoever can free us from birth and death. Amitābha Buddha, in his compassion and pity, made his vow with the fundamental intent of saving evil persons, so that they might be born in the West and attain Buddhahood. Is Amitābha Buddha compassionate? Too compassionate! We really must praise Amitābha Buddha (applause). The evil person who entrusts himself to the power of another is precisely the true cause of birth in the Pure Land; we need only single-mindedly take refuge in the saving power of Amitābha Buddha's name, and even though within our minds there are greed, anger, and delusion,
and we are evil persons,
still we
will absolutely be born in the Pure Land
(Note:

the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception, spoken from the golden mouth of our original teacher Śākyamuni Buddha and praised and upheld by Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, says:
“Sentient beings of few roots of goodness shall not be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.”
Yet the Original Vow school loudly advocates ‘evil persons as the true recipients’, taking evil as right and glorying in evil. This is māra-dharma, not Buddha-dharma!)

blocks.text: 2. Huijing and Master Jingzong Proclaim ‘Master Shandao's Pure Land Thought Is the Purest’: Their Real Aim Is to Promote the Original Vow School

inline.s: Their logic runs:
Master Shandao's Pure Land thought is the purest — Master Hōnen's transmission of Shandao's thought is the purest — Shinran's doctrine (the Original Vow school) is the summit
[Note: Is Master Hōnen's transmission of Shandao's thought really the purest?

Master Hōnen said that the ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ are the core of Shandao's thought. But what are the facts? The facts are: Master Shandao never spoke of a Gate of the Vast Vow at all; it was entirely fabricated by Master Hōnen
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)
. Nor did Master Shandao ever say that reciting the name brings certain birth; on the contrary, Master Shandao said: continuous recitation brings birth
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
and
The Eighteenth Vow
for details)

. The ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ that they invented themselves, they foist upon Master Shandao, falsely claiming this to be Master Shandao's Pure Land thought. Is this the purest way to ‘transmit’ Shandao's thought?
Is it the summit? See
How Hōnen and Others Distorted and Slandered Master Shandao
for details.

Master Huijing claims to rely solely on Master Shandao, patriarch of the Pure Land school, but in reality he flies the banner of the ‘Shandao lineage’ while relying chiefly on Japan's Master Hōnen and relying entirely on the doctrines of Shinran and others of the Japanese True Pure Land school (that is, the Original Vow school), promoting the Original Vow school. Master Jingzong took refuge under Master Huijing of Taiwan in 1996 and, following Master Huijing, devotes himself exclusively to spreading the Original Vow school.

Master Huijing, Preface to The Complete Works of Master Hōnen: “In the Pure Land teaching, Master Shandao's thought of Amitābha's Original Vow is the purest; and the one who loyally, reverently, and single-mindedly transmitted this thought, developing it in a manner pure and unmixed, concise and essential, steady and reliable, so that people felt as if the sun shone brightly, their minds opened and understood, and they joyfully accepted and practiced it — that one is Master Hōnen. Therefore this Complete Works of Master Hōnen is the essence of Pure Land doctrine and a mirror for practitioners; every chapter points straight to Amitābha's heart, every sentence reveals the original intent of deliverance. Master Shandao and Master Hōnen were both manifestations of Amitābha and Mahāsthāmaprāpta

(Note: Master Hōnen is actually extolled as a manifestation of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva! Master Hōnen's heretical teaching that ‘birth through scattered-mind recitation is the supreme Original Vow’ stands directly opposed to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva's
gather in all six faculties, and let pure mindfulness continue without interruption

” teaching; how could he be a reincarnation of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva? Master Hōnen fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow and distorted the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception, praised and upheld by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitābha Buddha) — a crime beyond pardon; how could he be a reincarnation of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva? These people dare to fabricate anything at all!
, and both entered samādhi in this very life
(Note: Master Hōnen himself admitted that he had not even attained single-mindedness
(see
Master Hōnen's Distortion of the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception
for details)
, and yet here he is extolled as having ‘entered samādhi in this very life’!
Thus the Original Vow school is nothing but fabrication.
Still, come to think of it, their patriarch Master Hōnen dared to fabricate even the Gate of the Vast Vow
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)
; so what would these disciples and grand-disciples not dare to fabricate?)

, and both were eminent in learning and wisdom; both took the Pure Land teaching as their exclusive school and Amitābha's Original Vow as their root; therefore their Pure Land thought is the orthodox lineage and the standard of the Pure Land school. If later scholars, good teachers, or anyone else, whose
written

works and arguments contradict these two patriarchs, then one should reject and not rely on them; for such scholars and good teachers are still ordinary beings who have not realized samādhi and whose wisdom and practice are incomplete, and their words, if not wholly in accord with the patriarchs (Shandao and Hōnen), will inevitably fall into so-called ‘separate understanding and separate practice’, setting up new meanings of their own; therefore they must not be followed.”
Moreover,

in his book A Collection of Passages on Birth from the Three Pure Land Sutras, Master Huijing extols the Original Vow school doctrine of Shinran, ‘the great master, the sage’ (the True Pure Land school), as the highest thought of the Pure Land school, and declares that ‘if one does not study and remains ignorant, one loses the great benefit of birth in the Pure Land’
A Collection of Passages on Birth from the Three Pure Land Sutras (by Master Shinran,
written,

translated by Master Huijing): “The Pure Land school takes the ‘Three Pure Land Sutras’ as its center, and the six fascicles of the Kyōgyōshinshō, which Master Shinran received through the treatises and commentaries of the seven patriarchs of the three countries, are their consummation. Therefore the transmission of the scriptures and the oral transmission of the master's work are its very life. The meaning of the Three Pure Land Sutras cannot be expounded except by a Śākyamuni who has greatly opened his perfect enlightenment, and cannot be known except by a bodhisattva who has entered the stage of assuredness. The three sutras take Bodhisattva Vasubandhu's Treatise on the Pure Land as the guide to their interpretation, and that treatise is made even clearer by Master Tanluan's Commentary on the Treatise on the Pure Land. To understand the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, one should use Master Shandao's Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra as a mirror; to understand the meaning of the Pure Land gate as a whole, there are Chan Master Daochuo's Collection of the Land of Peace and Bliss, Master Genshin's Collection on Birth in the Pure Land, and Master Hōnen's Senchakushū. Having mastered these scriptures, treatises, and commentaries,
one must reverently read the Kyōgyōshinshō (by Shinran,
authored
One should reflect on the meaning of the Shōshinge, recited in the morning and evening services (by Shinran,
authored

, and the words of sutra praises and so on, and ask a good teacher to explain their meaning. When the principle is clear and faith is deep — but if one does not study and remains ignorant, one loses the great benefit of birth in the Pure Land.”
Master Jingzong is a disciple who took refuge under Master Huijing, and naturally is no exception.

Master Jingzong, A Brief Exposition of the Amitābha Sutra: “Master Shandao was a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha; he devoted himself exclusively to practicing and spreading the Pure Land teaching, and is the great synthesizer of the Pure Land school, a great patriarch revered both in China and abroad, a great patriarch able to set the standard for past and present, the purest lineage of the Pure Land school.”

Master Jingzong, A Brief Exposition of Master Yinguang's Dharma Words: “Our Chinese Pure Land school has thirteen patriarchs. These thirteen patriarchs were recognized by later generations according to the extent of their influence in spreading the Pure Land teaching at the time; in terms of lineage transmission there are some differences, yet it is universally acknowledged that Master Shandao's thought on Buddha-recitation is the orthodox lineage of Chinese Pure Land...

Our Pure Land gate, relying on Master Shandao's correct interpretation and his teaching that sets the standard for past and present, will certainly not go astray. If you depart from Master Shandao, you are certainly impure, certainly mixed, certainly without supreme benefit, and certainly some people will fail to attain...
What the Pure Land school transmits is precisely Amitābha Buddha's Original Vow.”

Master Jingzong's Articles — Letters: “Though there are many teachers who spread the Pure Land teaching, one should rely exclusively on Monk Shandao; to mention Shandao in the same breath as other teachers is likewise to be ignorant of the teaching. Leaving the rest aside, simply consider Monk Shandao's
division of the two gates, the Essential Gate and the Vast Vow Gate
(Where did Master Shandao ever make such a division into ‘the two gates, Essential and Vast Vow’? This too was fabricated by Master Hōnen!
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)

, and his establishment of the two practices, right and miscellaneous, which embrace everything the other teachers said — how could anyone escape their scope, let alone rise above them? However profound and wondrous the other teachers' words may be, they remain within the expedient Essential Gate of the two good practices, meditative and non-meditative, and amount to dedicating merit and seeking birth; only Monk Shandao stands upon the Original Vow (the Vast Vow), relying wholly on the Buddha's power, for his is entirely a teaching of the fruition stage. The Buddha-recitation he teaches is neither meditative nor non-meditative; it is Original Vow recitation — ‘riding the Buddha's Original Vow and single-mindedly reciting exclusively’. Should later promoters of Buddha-recitation dare to deviate in the slightest from the track laid down by Monk Shandao, they are certainly impure!”
Master Jingzong not only inherits this doctrine but extols Master Huijing as ‘the foremost eye among gods and humans, the foremost guide of the Pure Land school’.

Master Jingzong's Articles — Letters: “The conclusion of Monk Shandao's Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra says: ‘Although the benefits of the two gates, meditative and non-meditative, have been explained above, in light of the Buddha's Original Vow, his intent for sentient beings is that they single-mindedly and exclusively recite Amitābha Buddha's name.’ This is the crowning point where the Original Vow school returns to its source, the very backbone and pillar of the Original Vow school... The Original Vow school of the Pure Land tradition takes exclusive recitation as its creed and discusses nothing else...

The Original Vow school is the confluence of the teachings on Amitābha's Original Vow spread by bodhisattvas, patriarchs, and good teachers of the three countries — India, China, and Japan — and it takes Monk Shandao's ‘exclusive recitation’ in particular as its creed.
The modern Master Huijing of the Pure Land school in Taiwan, the foremost eye among gods and humans, the foremost guide of the Pure Land school

(Note: Master Huijing is actually exalted as ‘the foremost eye among gods and humans, the foremost guide of the Pure Land school’! Where does this leave Master Shandao and Master Yongming, manifestations of Amitābha Buddha, and the other eleven patriarchs of the Pure Land school? Thus the Original Vow school is nothing but fabrication.
Still, come to think of it, their patriarch Master Hōnen dared to fabricate even the Gate of the Vast Vow
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)
, so what would these disciples and grand-disciples not dare to fabricate?

, who alone inherited a solitary lineage of a thousand years, drew deeply from the sources of three countries, and translated and compiled many precious texts, thereby expanding the great foundation of the teaching, spreading wide the net of the Original Vow teaching, and benefiting all living beings everywhere. That those of shallow capacity, hearing the sound of the Original Vow, are like jackals hearing the lion's roar, their hearts stricken with terror, fleeing with their heads in their hands — this is only to be expected. Yet those who recklessly utter evil words bring destruction upon themselves and obstruct others' wisdom-life; truly they are to be pitied and mourned.”
For related material, please refer to Master Yinguang: There Is No Division of ‘Pure and Impure’ Among the Pure Land Patriarchs' Doctrines

blocks.text: 3. The True Face of the Original Vow School: Annihilate All Dharmas and Keep Only Buddha-Recitation

inline.s: The article in Dharma Sound magazine mentions that the Original Vow school ‘holds that all miscellaneous practices such as giving, observing precepts, meditation, and diligence are a distrust of Amitābha Buddha, and advocates abandoning the sacred path’ — but this is only one point, the ‘abandoning of the sacred path’. In fact, as Hōnen himself said, ‘Abolish all vows and all practices; one should cultivate only the one vow and one practice of the West’, meaning that apart from the Eighteenth Vow and the single practice of exclusive Buddha-recitation, all the other great vows of Amitābha and other practices found in the Pure Land scriptures and treatises (chiefly the nine grades of birth in the Contemplation Sutra, practiced by dedicating various practices) should be abolished and abandoned!

Master Huijing, trans. and ed., The Collected Writings of Master Hōnen: “Those who wish to cultivate the karma of the Western Pure Land should be complete in the four practices and unmixed in the three karmas; abolish all vows and all practices, and cultivate only the one vow and one practice of the West.”
(The one vow and one practice
the Eighteenth Vow and the single practice of exclusive Buddha-recitation

Monk Huijing, A Brief Exposition of the Editor's Preface to A Record of Buddha-Recitation Responses: “Among the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, the wondrous Dharma suited to this place, this time, and these capacities is only ‘Amitābha's Original Vow and recitation of the name’. Although the Buddha-Dharma has eighty-four thousand gates, the only one that suits us criminal beings of the Sahā world in the Dharma-ending age is the single gate of recitation of the name by Amitābha's Original Vow. Let us consider for ourselves: apart from this gate, what other gate can bring us deliverance? Let us suppose that the six-character name were now taken away — however you might practice, could you be liberated? It is impossible to be liberated.”

Thus, for Master Hōnen and the Original Vow school, as the article in Dharma Sound magazine says, the Original Vow school holds that ‘the only hope is to rely on the Eighteenth Vow’. For related material, please refer to the article The Buddhist Association of China Refutes the Original Vow School: The Only Hope Is to Rely on the Eighteenth Vow.

Master Jingzong, The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao: “Abandon the sacred path and return to the Pure Land; lead the Essential Gate into the Vast Vow; abandon miscellaneous practices and return to right practice; set aside auxiliary karma and devote oneself to right concentration.” According to this book of Master Jingzong's, just as with Hōnen and Huijing, everything is abolished and discarded until only the single practice of Buddha-recitation and the single Eighteenth Vow remain.

Yang Renshan, in his Exposition of the Teaching, criticizes Master Hōnen's absurd classification of the teachings: “Kurodani (that is, Hōnen) classifies the bodhi mind and the six pāramitās and so on as miscellaneous practices, all of which should be abolished. If his words were true, then those who do not arouse the bodhi mind would be practicing rightly; if giving is abolished, the stingy and greedy would be practicing rightly; if precepts are abolished, the self-indulgent would be practicing rightly. Extending this, the wrathful, the lazy, the scattered, and the deluded would all be practicing rightly,
inverted teaching could go no further than this! It is as when worms in the lion's own body devour the lion's flesh. Thus we know that the Buddha-Dharma cannot be destroyed by outsiders!

‘Arousing the bodhi mind and cultivating all merits’ is taken to be ‘doubting the Buddha's wisdom’, whereas abolishing and discarding the bodhi mind and the six pāramitās and myriad practices, and turning to exclusive Buddha-recitation, alone counts as ‘deep faith in the Original Vow’ — no wonder Yang Renshan criticized their doctrine as ‘secretly harboring the seed of Dharma destruction’!
In his critique of The Principles of the True School, Yang Renshan also criticized the absurd doctrines of the True Pure Land school (the Original Vow school).

The Principles of the True School, no. 10, says: “The names ‘true’ and ‘conventional’ have layer upon layer of meaning. Our school provisionally takes the gate of settling the mind as the ultimate truth and the gate of human relations as the conventional truth.
Our school
(we of the True Pure Land school)
having permitted
(monks)
to keep wives

, cannot be without the five human relationships. Since there are the five relationships, one cannot but walk their way; this is the conventional truth. Though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with the power of the vow they are no more than a single grain in the ocean

(Though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with Amitābha Buddha's vow-power they are as a single grain of corn beside the great ocean, utterly insignificant. — For a refutation of this fallacy, see
Appendix 9:
Refuting ‘Reciting the Name Brings Certain Birth’ and ‘Evil Persons as the True Recipients’
therefore it does not ask whether
(a monk)
eats meat and keeps a wife
. The goodness of sentient beings is defiled; Amitābha's reward-land is undefiled,
and defiled goodness cannot be born into an undefiled land
Note: does this mean that only by doing evil can one be born in the undefiled land!?
Note: this is a brazen incitement to break the precepts and do evil. How could this be Buddha-Dharma?!

Yang Renshan comments: “What ‘no. 10’ says is entirely miscellaneous practice and miscellaneous cultivation. Why is it that the earlier passages vigorously sweep away all practices? Can it be that what is swept away is world-transcending practice, while what is not swept away is worldly practice?

Now worldly practice prolongs the karma of birth and death, while world-transcending practice goes against the stream of birth and death. Which is right and which is perverse, there must be those able to discern it. The gate of human relations is worldly goodness. If even worldly goodness is not abolished, why abolish world-transcending goodness alone?

All worldly goodness is encompassed within the bodhisattva's myriad practices. If one can dedicate it to the Pure Land, it becomes karma for birth there; otherwise it is merely a reward among gods and humans.
For one who has aroused the bodhi mind, all worldly goodness becomes undefiled
; for one who has not aroused the bodhi mind, even practicing the five pāramitās remains entirely defiled.”

Master Benhuan, There Is No Division of Pure and Impure Among the Pure Land Patriarchs: “Recently I have seen a student of the Pure Land teaching declare that among the patriarchs of the Pure Land school, Master Shandao alone is pure,
while the remaining twelve patriarchs are all impure

(Note: in the talks of Master Jingzong and others, even Master Yongming, a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha, is attacked as impure and lacking a lineage. Does this not make utterly clear what sort of stuff the Original Vow school really is?)
because they are entangled either with the Chan school or with the Tiantai

and Huayan schools. For instance, Master Yongming and Master Mengdong were both patriarchs of the Chan school, so their Pure Land teachings are impure. Master Lianchi was a patriarch of the Huayan school and a leading figure of Chan, so his teachings too are impure. Moreover, the three patriarchs Zhixu, Jieliu, and Sheng'an were all entangled with the Tiantai

and Chan schools, so their Pure Land teachings are all impure. And the recent Master Yinguang was also quite friendly with the Tiantai school, so his words too can hardly be pure. By ‘impure’ they mean that the teachings of these twelve patriarchs do not accord with Amitābha's Original Vow. Now, for the celebration of Amitābha Buddha's birthday, the Buddhist community takes the birthday of Master Yongming as the standard, because he is a manifestation of Amitābha.
Could it be that the words of Master Yongming, a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha, are instead not pure enough?

If you say Yongming's words are impure, then you are slandering Amitābha Buddha's teaching as impure. Further, the thirteenth patriarch, the recent Master Yinguang, is said to be a manifestation of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva; could Mahāsthāmaprāpta's words also be unworthy of trust? Such foolish views of deluded people are simply slander of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. Wishing to spread the Pure Land teaching, they instead destroy it.”

blocks.text: 4. The Frightfulness of Hōnen, the Original Vow School, Huijing, and Master Jingzong

inline.s: According to the doctrines of Master Hōnen, the Original Vow school, and Huijing and Master Jingzong of the so-called modern ‘Shandao lineage’, if only reliance on the Eighteenth Vow (exclusive Buddha-recitation) counts as ‘riding the Buddha's vow, according with the Buddha's Original Vow, and attaining certain birth’, then the other eighty-four thousand Dharma gates (practicing anything other than exclusive Buddha-recitation, and dedicating the merit to seek birth in the Pure Land) may — indeed must — be utterly swept away.

The Pure Land school, which was originally the refuge-gate where ‘no Dharma fails to flow forth from this gate, and no practice fails to return to it’, has been turned by various wrong views into a situation of irreconcilable hostility with the other eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, a fight to the death.

There are still nine thousand years left in the Dharma-ending age; that a single erroneous doctrine should cause the miserable state of the Dharma-ending age nine thousand years hence (when the scriptures and the Way are extinguished, and only the Immeasurable Life Sutra and a single Buddha-name remain in the world) to arrive ahead of time is something we students who spread the Pure Land teaching do not wish to see.

Advocating Buddha-recitation is good, but if one brazenly contradicts the scriptures and treatises and speaks at random, advocating Buddha-recitation at the cost of annihilating all Dharmas, then it is truly ‘wishing to spread the Pure Land, one instead destroys it’!
[The frightening thing about ‘Hōnen, the Original Vow school, Huijing, and Master Jingzong’ is this:
they destroy the Buddha's true Dharma!

Following their theories of inverted teaching and their schemes to exterminate all who differ, while abolishing the entire sacred-path gate (every gate other than the Pure Land teaching), they also slander the diligent, single-minded Buddha-recitation of those who practice as taught as ‘self-power recitation’ and abolish it; whereupon the Buddhist community becomes the exclusive domain of those who neither recite the Buddha-name diligently and single-mindedly, nor observe the precepts, nor cultivate merit, nor purify their own minds, and who even do evil all their lives (including slandering the true Dharma). Monks eat meat and keep wives and no longer even shave their heads, and they abandon the monastic robes for fear of public scrutiny when they break the precepts and do evil. In this way the true Saṅgha that is a model for gods and humans ceases to exist, and the masses, unable to obtain the true Buddha-Dharma and finding no effect in their practice, lose faith in the Buddha-Dharma. What a scene this is! (For such a scene, see
The Practice of Master Hōnen's Teaching
for details
.) Therefore the great layman Yang Renshan criticized them: “
secretly harboring the seed of Dharma destruction
It is as when worms in the lion's own body devour the lion's flesh. Thus we know that the Buddha-Dharma cannot be destroyed by outsiders!

[Worms in the lion's own body devour the lion's flesh] This means: these people support themselves by the Buddha-Dharma, yet do not know to repay the Buddha's kindness, and instead turn around and destroy the Buddha-Dharma. How shameful and hateful this is! [Thus we know that the Buddha-Dharma cannot be destroyed by outsiders] This means: the Buddha-Dharma can be destroyed only by these māra's children and grandchildren hidden within the Buddhist community, striking from within — this is māra's only means of destroying the Buddha-Dharma. When Śākyamuni Buddha was in the world, Māra said he would destroy the Buddha-Dharma, and the Buddha replied: What I teach is the true Dharma; no one can destroy it. Māra then said: In your Dharma-ending age, I will have all my descendants leave home, don the robe, and destroy your Dharma. Hearing this, the Buddha wept, and there was nothing he could do.

These destroyers of the Buddha's true Dharma are truly beyond reason, and they never consider the karmic retribution of what they do! Nor do their followers and supporters consider the fate of those who serve as the tiger's ghouls!
In the Sutra of the Buddha's Treasury,

Chapter Seven, ‘Former Ages’, the Buddha spoke of the karmic retribution of those who in former times destroyed the Buddha's true Dharma, together with their followers, supporters, and backers, saying:
These evil persons
destroy the Buddha's true Dharma

, and bring great ruin and affliction upon many people. Again, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avīci Hell, lying face upward for nine million billion years, face downward for nine million billion years, on the left side
(lying on the left side)
for nine million billion years, on the right side
(lying on the right side)

for nine million billion years, burned and charred upon hot iron. Dying and passing from there, they are reborn in the Roasting Hell, the Great Roasting Hell, the Revival Hell, and the Black Rope Hell, suffering all manner of affliction for the same number of years. Dying in the Black Rope Hell, they are born again in the great Avīci Hell.
Śāriputra,
for this reason, whether lay or monastic, those who draw near to such a person
(the followers of these evil persons)
, and good teachers
(the backers of these evil persons)
and the various donors
(the almsgivers and supporters of these evil persons)
, six hundred and four trillion people in all, together with these four teachers
(with these four evil persons)
, are born and die together and undergo burning and boiling in the great hell
. Thus, Śāriputra,

all the households of good teachers, the households of donors, the disciples, the teachers, and the compliant practitioners connected with such a person — all who are numbered among them — are born in hell

Śāriputra, you cannot know their number; only the Tathāgata can know it. Those who are born and die together with such an evil person in the great hell number six hundred and four trillion, and thus for a kalpa they undergo suffering; when the great kalpa is burned, they remain in hell. Why is this? Śāriputra, to destroy the Tathāgatas' supreme perfect enlightenment is a crime most heavy, not light. When the great kalpa is burned, these four evil persons and the six hundred and four trillion people pass from this great Avīci Hell and are reborn in other regions, in great hells. Why is this? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses are complete and their retribution is no small matter; in those other regions they undergo great suffering for countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of years. When the world comes into being again, these four criminals and the six hundred and four trillion people, together with others whose offenses are not yet exhausted, at the end of their lives there are born again in the great hell here.”
[To serve as the tiger's ghoul (
chāng
) — to act as the ghoul of a tiger. In ancient lore, those eaten by a tiger became ghouls after death, whose sole task was to lure people to be eaten by the tiger.

blocks.text: Appendix 3: A Heterodox Path Attached to Buddhism: The Original Vow School (Excerpts)

inline.s: A heterodox path attached to Buddhism in which ‘spreading the Dharma’ becomes a pursuit of wealth and ‘taking disciples’ resembles a pyramid scheme: the Original Vow school.

A Buddhist friend online, Brother Zhaoxuan, once saw with his own eyes: they have now encroached upon the eastern Sichuan area. Their condition is that joining with them brings financial gain. Many students of Buddhism think this is the practice of the Pure Land, and even some great monks have been drawn in, running fast-food-style ‘Dharma spreading’. Because this model brings in a lot of money, it also quickly produces many great ‘Dharma masters’, and some poor temples have used this money to build halls and dormitories — a strong tendency to treat whoever supplies the milk as one's mother.
I once heard a ‘Dharma master’ of the Original Vow faction give a talk; before several hundred people, hoarse with shouting, he told them:
“By coming today to hear this talk, you have already obtained your ticket to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss!”

(Note: this is the Original Vow school fabricating nonsense to deceive the faithful! Hear one talk of his and you have already obtained your ticket to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss?! Our original teacher Śākyamuni Buddha taught the sutras and expounded the Dharma for forty-nine years — and that counts for less than one talk of theirs? In the Buddha Speaks of the Immeasurable Life Buddha Sutra, the Buddha says:
“Though for one lifetime you labor and suffer, in but a moment you will afterwards be born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where bliss has no limit.”
At the end of the sutra, the Buddha earnestly admonishes:
“You should believe and comply,
and practice in accordance with the Dharma

Yet the Original Vow school says, ‘By coming today to hear this talk, you have already obtained your ticket to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss!’ Fabricating nonsense and inverting the teaching to such a degree — this is the Original Vow school! Utterly, thoroughly heretical!!!)
And they also wildly attack and exclude other Dharma gates and Dharma masters.

(Note: this is the Original Vow school exterminating all who differ! ‘Self-power recitation’, ‘practice of the Essential Gate’, ‘the impure Pure Land school’, ‘the pseudo-Pure Land school’ — these are the terms they habitually use when exterminating those who differ.)

Then the laypeople answer in unison: Amitābha! All of this is led by specially trained core cadres. From place to place they follow these Dharma masters, turning ‘spreading the Dharma’ into a pursuit of wealth. It has become like an illegal pyramid scheme!

The Original Vow school dismembers the Pure Land scriptures and teachings, declaring that one need only believe in the power of Amitābha's Original Vow to obtain at once a passport to birth in the Pure Land — no need to observe precepts, no need to do good, no need to arouse the bodhi mind, no need to practice the bodhisattva path, no need to repent; even if one has killed people and set fires, at the time of death one will certainly be born there. The Original Vow school proclaims a doctrine of pure other-power, denying self-power (holding that once one believes in the Original Vow school, the Buddha will naturally liberate one, without any effort of one's own, without giving, precepts, or even supporting one's parents), proclaiming that ‘another acts and I receive’ (the matter of birth has already been accomplished for me by the Buddha; I need only believe), opposing karmic retribution (
all the evil one has done is borne by the Buddha on my behalf
), opposing ‘one reaps what one sows’ (
whatever evil one does
, so long as one believes in Amitābha's Original Vow,
the Buddha will surely bear it for me
, with no effect at all on one's birth in the Pure Land).
(Note: these are the marks of the Original Vow school: inverted teaching and incitement to break the precepts and do evil.)
In this way the Original Vow school becomes the most convenient and easiest gate of liberation in the world.
In Japan,
the monastics of the Original Vow faction
, because it suffices to believe in Amitābha's Original Vow and recite a single invocation of Amitābha Buddha,
with no need to observe precepts, no need to practice the six pāramitās, no need to arouse the bodhi mind, may marry and have children, may eat meat and drink wine,
and so they are all
professional monks
. By day they stay in the temple, drawing lots and telling fortunes for people, and liberating the dead,
and at night they go home
to enjoy the pleasures of family life.
[Note: where is there still a true Saṅgha that is a model for gods and humans? On what does the Buddha's true Dharma rest? The Buddha says:
“The future destruction of the true Dharma will not come from the ruin wrought by heavenly māras and outside paths, but from the corruption and collapse of the Saṅgha!”
(On the Treasure of the Saṅgha)
The corruption and collapse of the Saṅgha is the inevitable result of Master Hōnen's teaching. Be on guard! The overturned cart ahead is a lesson for the cart behind.
[The overturned cart ahead is a lesson for the cart behind] The fact that the cart in front has overturned is a warning for the cart behind.

This runs entirely counter to the fine traditions of Chinese Buddhism — ‘monastic dress, vegetarian diet, celibacy, and observance of precepts’. Both in form and in content, the Original Vow school is a degeneration of Buddhism. Even in Japan, the Original Vow faction has been criticized by many other Buddhist schools.

I truly cannot understand how such a religious monstrosity should find so many people in our country eagerly spreading it, with some monastics taking part as well, scattering materials about the Original Vow school everywhere,
calling for reform of Chinese Buddhist tradition and loudly demanding that we learn from Japanese Buddhism and from the Original Vow school
. They think that such a fine, effortless, easily accomplished supreme Amitābha as the Original Vow school offers should have been discovered by none of the patriarchs of China through the ages!

There is no doubt that what those who eagerly spread the Original Vow school, and those who eagerly proclaim that we should learn from Japanese Buddhism, really want is simply to cast off the fine traditions of Chinese Buddhism (traditions that are a restraint upon those who only pretend to practice), so that they may, like the monks of Japan's Original Vow faction, both openly enjoy the five desires of the world and obtain liberation after death, both rightfully receive the faithful's offerings and worship and live comfortably, and be free from labor and worry about livelihood; as for reforming Buddhism and revitalizing Buddhism, that is merely their pretext.

(Note: to satisfy their private desires, these people destroy the Buddha's true Dharma in this way, never considering their own future retribution! And the most pitiable and most unfortunate are the faithful who are kept in the dark, following them in confusion to create the karma (of destroying the Buddha's true Dharma) and receive its retribution (falling into the Avīci Hell for long kalpas).)

This is the mentality of lazy folk who love ease and hate labor. In terms of mentality, it is these people who are the ones the Buddha spoke of, the ones we in this final age must truly guard against: the
worms in the lion's body

blocks.text: Appendix 4: What Is the Difference Between Japan's Original Vow School and the Pure Land School (Excerpts)

inline.s: First we must understand what
the essential purpose of Buddhism
is, namely
“Do no evil, practice all good, and purify one's own mind”

In the Pure Land school, ‘purifying one's own mind’ is accomplished by the method of Buddha-recitation, while ‘doing no evil and practicing all good’ is accomplished through the three blessings of pure karma; Buddha-recitation as the primary practice is the right practice, and observing precepts, doing good, and cultivating various merits as the auxiliary is the assisting practice.

The Original Vow school of pure other-power holds that one need only believe in Amitābha Buddha and recite the Buddha-name a few times with a grateful mind; precepts, doing good, and all the rest are unnecessary — leave it all to Amitābha Buddha, and he will pull you there. It does not matter if you go on doing evil; moreover, as Japan's
