Shinran said, founder of the True Pure Land school: among those who equally believe in Amitābha, it is the evildoers who are the true cause of attaining Buddhahood, while doing good is a mixed poison, a distrust of the Buddha's power, making birth in the Pure Land difficult. He even said that if you recite Amitābha and then go kill three thousand people, you can still be born there
. Under the influence of such thinking, Japanese Buddhism violated the Buddha's final instruction to ‘take the precepts as your teacher’,
openly indulging in eating, drinking, whoring, and gambling
, and declined day by day. The Original Vow faction among them even became an accomplice in Japan's invasion of China,
declaring that killing Chinese people could bring birth in the Pure Land

Although the Pure Land school speaks of exclusive Pure Land practice, it respects the other schools. The Original Vow school (Japan's True Pure Land school), by contrast, openly declares that the sacred-path gate must be abolished (all other Dharma gates, and even the joint cultivation of right and assisting practices such as the six pāramitās and myriad practices).

From this it can be seen that the key difference between the Original Vow school and the Pure Land school lies in the question of whether one should observe precepts and do good, and whether one should arouse the bodhi mind! The spread of the Original Vow school may in the short term attract some people to recite the Buddha-name, which is of some benefit, but in the long run, given human laziness, this lazy method will easily come to dominate everything, and the result will be that Buddhism as a whole inevitably loses its fundamental spirit of compassion; having lost ‘do no evil, practice all good’,
Buddhism will exist in name only, a mere empty shell
(Note: this is māra's means of destroying the Buddha-Dharma — breaking through from within!)

Moreover, if one distorts the Buddha's intent and mistakes Amitābha's compassionate vow-power for an umbrella protecting evildoing, one will undoubtedly fall into the Avīci Hell, never to escape for myriad kalpas! Furthermore, Buddha-recitation requires arousing the bodhi mind, and the bodhi mind means ‘seeking the Buddha's way above and transforming beings below’. One must have a true vow to be born in the Pure Land, a willingness to go to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and attain Buddhahood; otherwise, when at the time of death karmic forces suddenly appear and one clings to life and fears death, unable to let go of this or that, unwilling to go, one's consciousness reeling and confused, one's hands and feet in a fluster, and one may even have long forgotten the Buddha-name — would Amitābha, who ‘forever accords with sentient beings’, drag you there by force?
(Note: since one cannot be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, then to which destiny will one go? And what will the following many lives and many kalpas be like? Think deeply! Think deeply!)

blocks.text: Appendix 5: The Threefold Abolition and Establishment of the Original Vow School

inline.s: The faith in the Buddha's Original Vow advocated by the Original Vow school stresses only one vow among Amitābha's Original Vows and ignores the teachings elsewhere in the scriptures,
and even uses this to tell people that killing and arson do not matter, that it is fine for monks to marry and have children, and that drinking wine and eating meat are all acceptable

(Note: such statements invert the teaching and incite people to break the precepts and do evil; this is a mark of the Original Vow school. The Original Vow school has three great marks of destroying the Buddha's true Dharma: first, inverted teaching; second, inciting people to break the precepts and do evil; third, exterminating all who differ.)
In fact, this falls within the category of slandering the Dharma, which the Buddha specially reiterated.
The Original Vow school loudly proclaims
“the threefold abolition and establishment”
(Note: this is a mark of the Original Vow school: exterminating all who differ, so that the Buddhist community becomes the exclusive domain of heretical teachings and evil people.)
The abolition and establishment of sacred path and Pure Land:
abandon the sacred path and establish the Pure Land's expedient path;
(The first level: abolishing and establishing among the various Buddhist schools,
exterminating all schools other than the Pure Land school, including Chan, Esoteric, Vinaya, and Southern Buddhism, leaving only the Pure Land school.)
The abolition and establishment of inner and outer:
abandon inner power (abandon self-power) and establish outer power (establish other-power);

(The second level: abolishing and establishing within the one surviving Pure Land school, leaving only the Original Vow school. The Original Vow school absurdly divides Buddha-recitation into self-power recitation and other-power recitation. Those who end evil and do good, who are single-minded and diligent in recitation, are labeled ‘self-power recitation’ and slandered as distrusting Amitābha Buddha, and it is said of them that ‘they cannot be born in the Pure Land, or can only with difficulty be born there, or at best will be born in the borderland city of doubt’

; while the lazy and indolent, those who break the precepts and do evil, are instead described as practitioners of ‘other-power recitation’ who absolutely trust Amitābha Buddha, and it is said that these are the ones whom Amitābha's deliverance is aimed at, that this is Amitābha's supreme Original Vow, and that these ‘other-power recitation’ practitioners will all certainly be born in the Land of Perfect Reward and Adornment. — Inverted teaching could go no further! What is more, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others wildly attack the patriarchs of our Chinese Pure Land school (including Master Yongming, a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha), calling them impure, without lineage, and so on, while loudly extolling Master Hōnen's transmission of Shandao's thought as the purest and Shinran's doctrine (the Original Vow school) as the summit, in a vain attempt to install Hōnen and Shinran as the orthodoxy of the Pure Land school in our country!)
: The abolition and establishment of true and false:

abandon the false expedients of the nineteenth vow, the twentieth vow, the Contemplation Sutra, and the Amitābha Sutra, and establish the true reality of the eighteenth vow of the Immeasurable Life Sutra.

(The third level: abolishing and establishing among the Buddha's sutras (what outrageous audacity)! First they abolish the Contemplation Sutra and the Amitābha Sutra, leaving only the Immeasurable Life Sutra; then they abolish and establish within the contents of the Immeasurable Life Sutra (they especially hate and fear the Buddha's teaching in the Immeasurable Life Sutra concerning

the ‘five evils, five pains, and five burnings’, because it stabs them where it hurts), leaving only the eighteenth vow; and then they distort the eighteenth vow to mean: reciting the name brings certain birth. With such abolitions and establishments, what has the Buddha-Dharma become? The World-Honored One labored for forty-nine years teaching the sutras and expounding the Dharma, the three baskets and twelve divisions — and all of it is to be destroyed in a single blow by these dregs of the Buddhist order! Can their scheme be allowed to succeed?)

[Note: their wishful calculation is that after these three abolitions and establishments, the result will be that only the Original Vow school and the eighteenth vow, distorted by them into ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’, remain. Moreover, they admonish their disciples, grand-disciples, and the faithful to read only the works of Hōnen, Shinran, and the like. In this way the Buddhist community becomes the exclusive domain of their heretical teachings and heretical faction,
and the Buddha's true Dharma is destroyed

The Original Vow school distorts the ‘even ten recitations’ of the eighteenth vow — the only vow they retain — into meaning ten scattered-minded recitations of the Buddha-name in ordinary times. Hence they advocate ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’, and therefore no need to observe precepts, no need to cultivate merit, no need to purify one's own mind, and even a lifetime of evildoing does not matter; and they proclaim ‘evil persons as the true recipients’. Yet those who practice in accordance with the Three Pure Land Sutras they brand with such crimes as ‘self-power recitation’, ‘practice of the Essential Gate’, ‘the impure Pure Land school’, and ‘the pseudo-Pure Land school’, and exterminate them.

Moreover, the Amitābha Sutra is the ‘sutra protected and remembered by all Buddhas’ (including, of course, Amitābha Buddha), praised by all Buddhas (including, of course, Amitābha Buddha). In the Amitābha Sutra, Śākyamuni Buddha says:
In the Western world
there is the Buddha of Immeasurable Life,

the Buddha of Immeasurable Marks, the Buddha of Immeasurable Banners, the Buddha of Great Light, the Buddha of Great Clarity, the Buddha of Jeweled Marks, and the Buddha of Pure Light; Buddhas numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each in his own land, extending his broad and long tongue, covering the three thousand great thousand worlds, and speaking these truthful words: You sentient beings,
should believe in this sutra of praising inconceivable merit
which is protected and remembered by all Buddhas
This
sutra protected and remembered by all Buddhas

is actually slandered by them as a ‘false expedient’ and abolished. Slandering the Buddha and destroying the Dharma could go no further than this! Can such people be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss? On the contrary, the blazing fires of hell await them!

Master Shandao was a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha; throughout his life he vigorously advocated receiving and upholding the Buddha Speaks of Amitābha Buddha Sutra, personally copying more than a hundred thousand scrolls to distribute to his disciples and the faithful, urging them to practice as taught (see
The Biography of Master Shandao (Vernacular and Original Text)
for details). This precisely shows that this
sutra protected and remembered by all Buddhas
” is the fundamental basis for study and practice in the Pure Land school. Yet Hōnen, Huijing, Jingzong, and others have slandered this
sutra protected and remembered by all Buddhas
as a ‘false expedient’ and abolished it. Moreover, Master Hōnen deliberately distorted
the Tang translation of the Amitābha Sutra, the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception (see
“Master Hōnen's Distortion of the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception”
for details). This
fully proves that their so-called ‘reliance on Master Shandao’ and ‘inheriting Master Shandao's Pure Land thought’
, and ‘spreading Master Shandao's Pure Land thought’, are all entirely false! And they even advertise themselves as the ‘Shandao lineage’!
Such claims can find no basis whatsoever in the Buddhist scriptures; they are a great wrong view that carves up the sutras and distorts the patriarchs' original intent.

The Original Vow school vigorously proclaims that among Amitābha's Original Vows, one particular vow is the key, the ‘Original Vow’. Shinran, the founder of the Original Vow school, declared: The Tathāgata appears in the world solely to proclaim the ocean of Amitābha's Original Vow. These are absolutely words that slander the true Dharma. Are all the other sutras the Buddha taught then mere nonsense?
That the Buddha-Dharma's gates should be abolished and established by ordinary people themselves!
That this is a wrong view slandering the true Dharma is beyond doubt.
Second,
the Original Vow school proclaims that merits and causes are all bestowed by the Buddha rather than cultivated by oneself
(Note: this is a mark of the Original Vow school: inverted teaching.)

It proclaims that once one believes, one's merit is sufficient. This is an utterly absurd theory. For if one truly believed, how could one not believe in the three blessings of pure karma taught by the Buddha? How could one not believe in the three refuges, the five precepts, and the ten wholesome deeds taught by the Buddha?
Finally, the most crucial point. The Amitābha Sutra says:
“Śāriputra, one cannot be born in that land with few roots of goodness and merits and causes.”

Yet the Original Vow school says that if you merely believe and wish to be born there, your roots of goodness, merits, and causes are sufficient. This is in fact a colossal lie, fabricated by them! Who told you that once you believe, your merits and causes are complete? Without merit, it is indeed possible that one may not even hear the Pure Land teaching. But is hearing it enough for merit to suffice? This is merely their own speculation.

From the various scriptures it can be seen that roots of goodness refer to: non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion. These three roots give rise to all wholesome dharmas, and are therefore called roots of goodness. It is by no means the case that merely hearing the Buddha's name once means one's roots of goodness are sufficient.
A monastic who never abstains from killing, who drinks wine and eats meat, who violates the precepts, and who marries and has children
(It really makes one laugh one's teeth off — that there should be monastics in the world who marry and have children! What kind of ‘leaving home’ is this?)
— how many roots of goodness can he have? A person who everywhere discourages others from observing precepts and doing good
(Note: this is a mark of the Original Vow school: inciting people to break the precepts and do evil.)
— how many roots of goodness can he have? It goes without saying.
Whether or not one has roots of goodness can be known simply by seeing whether one has any desire to practice wholesome deeds.

Most laughably, the Original Vow school even uses the birth in the Pure Land of the lowest-grade beings in the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life to prove that those who slander the true Dharma and commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evils
can all be born in the Pure Land
Note: this is a mark of the Original Vow school: inverted teaching.)

Yet they ignore the exception in the great vow: ‘except those who slander the true Dharma and commit the five heinous crimes’. They take the case in which, at the point of death, one has special circumstances, someone helps and reminds one, and one is able to recite the Buddha-name in ten uninterrupted thoughts,
and exaggerate it into the claim that all who commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evils can do the same!

blocks.text: Appendix 6: What Is the Original Vow School (Excerpts)

inline.s: Question: What is the Original Vow school?

Answer: When Amitābha Buddha was the monk Dharmākara in ages past, he made forty-eight vows to accomplish the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and to save all sentient beings. The eighteenth of these is called Amitābha's Original Vow. The eighteenth vow is:

“If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions, with sincere minds of faith and joy, wish to be born in my land and recite even ten thoughts — if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment. Excepted are those who commit the five heinous crimes and slander the true Dharma.”
(See the Buddha Speaks of the Immeasurable Life Sutra.)
Here
the ‘even ten thoughts’ spoken of in the eighteenth vow
means ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death
. For its basis, see
The Eighteenth Vow
for details.

The distinguishing feature of the Original Vow school is that it distorts the ‘even ten thoughts’ of the eighteenth vow into ten scattered-minded recitations of the Buddha-name in ordinary times. Hence they advocate ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ (that one need only recite the Buddha-name casually in ordinary times and at death one will certainly be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss), and therefore no practice is needed, no precepts need be observed, no good need be done, no purification of one's own mind is needed, and even a lifetime of evildoing does not matter, because ‘evil persons are the true recipients of Amitābha's deliverance’. (This is completely and utterly inverted teaching!
For a refutation of this fallacy, see
Appendix 9:
Refuting ‘Reciting the Name Brings Certain Birth’ and ‘Evil Persons as the True Recipients’

Originally, the Original Vow school in China and the Original Vow school in Japan are cut from the same cloth: their theories both derive from Master Hōnen and Master Shinran, and the content they advocate is identical (except that the Chinese Original Vow school is better at concealment and less barefaced). But the Japanese Original Vow school founded by Master Hōnen and Master Shinran has such a foul reputation that Master Huijing of the so-called ‘Pure Land school’ in Taiwan and Master Jingzong of Hongyuan Temple on the mainland tried to deceive the faithful of our country by giving it a new face. Master Huijing said: “So our gate is not some Japanese Pure Land (gate),
our Original Vow school

is the gate of Amitābha Buddha's eighteenth vow.” (See Master Huijing: What Exactly Is the Lineage of the Original Vow School?) Thus the Original Vow school now comes in a Chinese version and a Japanese version, though this is only the same brew in a different cup.
For Japan's Original Vow school, see
The Practice of Master Hōnen's Teaching
Do Not Promote Japan's Original Vow School

, and other articles. As for the Chinese Original Vow school, they no longer dare to fly the banner of Master Hōnen and Master Shinran, so they fly the banner of ‘relying on Master Shandao’ to peddle ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ and ‘
the doctrine of evil persons as the true recipients
’. In reality, all their words and deeds are thoroughly opposed to Master Shandao; see
How Hōnen and Others Distorted and Slandered Master Shandao

for details. And this ‘Chinese Original Vow school’ of theirs likewise distorts the ‘even ten thoughts’ of the eighteenth vow into ten recitations in ordinary times, and likewise advocates: reciting the name brings certain birth; no need to observe precepts, no need to cultivate merit, no need to purify one's own mind, and even a lifetime of evildoing does not matter, because ‘evil persons are the true recipients of Amitābha's deliverance’. (See Master Jinghui's Essential Meaning of the Pure Land School and Master Jingzong's The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao, Master Jingzong's Buddhist Web Interview, and other books and statements.) As for the so-called ‘seven patriarchs of three countries’ (
India's Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna and Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, China's Master Tanluan, Chan Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao, and Japan's Bishop Genshin and Master Hōnen

), the ‘abolition of the Essential Gate and establishment of the Vast Vow Gate’, ‘another acts and I receive’ (the matter of birth has already been accomplished for me by Amitābha, and I need only believe), the denial of karmic retribution (all the evil one has done is borne by Amitābha on my behalf), the denial of ‘one reaps what one sows’ (whatever evil one does, so long as one believes in Amitābha's Original Vow, Amitābha will surely bear it for me, with no effect at all on one's birth in the Pure Land), and the doctrine of evil persons as the true recipients (that Amitābha's deliverance takes evil persons as its true recipients) — which of these does not originate in Japan's Original Vow school? Even the trick of flying the banner of ‘relying on Master Shandao’ to deceive the faithful was picked up from Master Hōnen and Master Shinran. Moreover, in Master Huijing's translation of Shinran's A Collection of Passages on Birth from the Three Pure Land Sutras,
he extols the Original Vow school doctrine of Hōnen and Shinran (the True Pure Land school) as the highest thought of the Pure Land school

, and declares that ‘if one does not study and remains ignorant, one loses the great benefit of birth in the Pure Land’. Master Huijing's followers, in turn, extol Shinran's A Collection of Passages on Birth from the Three Pure Land Sutras as ‘the Light of the Land of Ultimate Bliss’.

Here let us also mention, in passing, the origins of Master Huijing's and Master Jingzong's connection with Japan's Original Vow school. Master Huijing (of Taiwan) lived alone in the mountains in solitary practice beginning in the spring of 1985, for three years. During this time he read Master Hōnen's Senchakushū, the Collection on Choosing Original Vow Buddha-Recitation,
“and knew that the Pure Land teaching should take the Shandao lineage
(the so-called ‘Shandao lineage’ is simply Master Hōnen's system of teaching, according to which Master Hōnen's disciple Master Shinran established Japan's Original Vow school)

as the purest, according with Amitābha's original intent of saving beings above and with all the capacities of sentient beings below. In the autumn of 1988 he traveled to study at Ōtani University in Kyoto, Japan
(Ōtani University is a private university founded by Japan's True Pure Land school, that is, Japan's Original Vow school)
, studying the Shandao-line Pure Land thought
(‘Shandao-line Pure Land thought’ is another name for the ‘True School studies’ of Japan's Original Vow school, and ‘True School studies’ is Ōtani University's foremost course)
(The above is taken from their own Brief Biography of Master Huijing.) Master Huijing's disciple Master Xinyuan also wrote in an open letter replying to Master Jingzong: “
Strictly speaking, we
(that is, Master Xinyuan, Master Jingzong, and others)
have also received the grace of the True School's teaching. Our study of the Original Vow comes from our revered teacher
(Master Huijing)
, and our revered teacher learned it in Japan, steeped in the True School for three years.

[Note: these words make perfectly clear the transmission relationship between the Chinese Original Vow school led by Master Huijing and the Japanese Original Vow school whose patriarchs are Hōnen and Shinran.]

Thus Master Huijing went in person to the private university of Japan's Original Vow school to ‘seek the Way’, and received his lineage from Japan's Original Vow school (see also his Essential Meaning of the Pure Land School, written after his return from Japan). Master Jingzong (of the mainland) took refuge under Master Huijing in 1996 and vigorously promoted the Original Vow school on the mainland (which they euphemistically call ‘vigorously spreading Master Shandao's Buddha-recitation teaching on the mainland’), reaching every province.

Amusingly, the Chinese Original Vow school led by Master Huijing actually takes its lineage from Japan's Original Vow school and regards Master Hōnen and Master Shinran as its founding patriarchs, yet everywhere it seeks to ‘draw a clear line’ between itself and Japan's Original Vow school, Hōnen, and Shinran — one might call this deceiving one's teachers and extinguishing one's ancestors. From this its falsity is all the more evident!

[Note: the Chinese Original Vow school led by Master Huijing, seeing that the name ‘Original Vow school’ stinks so badly, does not dare to use it openly and often replaces it with ‘relying on Master Shandao’, ‘spreading Master Shandao's Pure Land thought’, or ‘spreading Master Shandao's Buddha-recitation teaching’
. Yet Master Shandao has three extremely important teachings: first, the two practices, right and assisting; second, continuous recitation brings birth; third, right mindfulness at the time of death.
(See
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
for details
In these three teachings Master Shandao gives a clear exposition of how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; this is
Master Shandao's Pure Land teaching
. Yet in the ‘Dharma words of Master Shandao’ compiled by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong
(see The Complete Works of Master Shandao, compiled and narrated by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong and published by Jingzong Press in 2005)
, they
dare not include them

, for fear of revealing their true colors. This fully proves that their reliance on Master Shandao is false, and that they fly the banner of ‘reliance’ to peddle their own private goods; it also fully proves that the ‘Pure Land thought of Master Shandao’ they promote is not the true Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, but something forged from their own private goods — just watch the video The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao
(lectured by Master Jingzong in 2006)
and you will know.
In his
forty-three-episode lecture series The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao,
Master Jingzong says over and over that
the ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ are the core of Master Shandao's Pure Land thought. But what are the facts? The facts are:
Master Shandao never spoke of a Gate of the Vast Vow at all; it was entirely fabricated by Master Hōnen
(see
Master Hōnen Fabricated the Gate of the Vast Vow
for details)
. Nor did Master Shandao ever say that reciting the name brings certain birth; on the contrary, Master Shandao said: continuous recitation brings birth
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
for details)

The ‘Gate of the Vast Vow’ and ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ that they fabricated themselves, they foist upon Master Shandao, falsely claiming this to be Master Shandao's Pure Land thought. Is this how one spreads Master Shandao's Pure Land thought?

These three teachings of Master Shandao (‘the two practices, right and assisting’, ‘continuous recitation brings birth’, and ‘right mindfulness at the time of death’) are a demon-revealing mirror. Hold the words of Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others up against it, and whether they rely on Master Shandao, whether they spread Master Shandao's Pure Land thought, whether they spread Master Shandao's Buddha-recitation teaching — true or false, right or heretical — will be seen at once.]

blocks.text: Appendix 7: Statement by Master Rende, President of the Jiuhua Mountain Buddhist Association

inline.s: To the Buddhist Association of China:

The ‘Original Vow school’ claims to originate from the Buddhist Pure Land school and to be a branch of Japan's True Pure Land school; because its rules and doctrines are vastly different from, indeed run counter to, the Pure Land school in the true sense, it is in fact using the Buddhist banner to spread its own preachings, and it has created an extremely vile influence in the Buddhist circles of our country!
Shi Shengsu, one of those who spread the ‘Original Vow school’
now renamed Master Jingzong, who went off to take refuge under Master Huijing of Taiwan, who advocates the Original Vow school

, was once a disciple of this poor monk. After receiving the precepts in 1997, because he did not observe the temple rules and repeatedly refused to heed advice, he then left the mountain without permission to spread heretical teachings, and his whereabouts remain unknown to this day. Having learned that for many years Shi Shengsu has continued to use the name of a Jiuhua Mountain disciple to spread heretical teachings and confuse people everywhere, I find it truly heartbreaking that a disciple of the Buddhist order should do such a thing as deceiving his teacher and extinguishing his ancestors. In order to implement the spirit of the notice Chi(zhou City) Zong(Religious Affairs Bureau) No. 2000-29, ‘On Forwarding the Provincial Religious Affairs Bureau Office's Forwarding of the National Religious Affairs Bureau's Report on Questions Concerning Japan's “Original Vow School”’, to preserve the purity of the Buddhist order, and to protect the true Dharma, I solemnly declare: I sever the relationship of teacher and disciple with Shi Shengsu, and henceforth all his illegal acts have nothing to do with Jiuhua Mountain. Rende, President of the Jiuhua Mountain Buddhist Association, December 21, 2000
(Originally published in Sweet Dew, 2001, issue 1, whole no. 36)

blocks.text: Appendix 8: The Original Vow School Is a Crooked Path and Heretical Way

inline.s: Recorded from ‘Elder Weixian's Teaching to the Chanting Team of the Buddha-Recitation Society of Guangde Temple, Suining, Sichuan’
[Original editor's note]
Master Jingzong

was originally a disciple of Master Rende of Jiuhua Mountain. His original name was Shengsu; because he spread Japan's Original Vow school, Master Rende later announced the severing of their teacher-disciple relationship. Japan's Original Vow school has been refuted by eminent monks and great virtue of the Pure Land school, and some Dharma masters have called it a heretical teaching.

There is now a crooked path and heretical way, namely Japan's Original Vow school; let me tell you about it. The Original Vow school comes from Japan. In Kyoto, Japan, there is an Eastern Hongwanji Temple and also a Western Hongwanji Temple, built by the Japanese True School. Who is the patriarch of the Japanese True School?
His name is Shinran
His way of life was to drink wine and eat meat, and he took a wife.

More than ninety percent of today's Japanese monks, one may say, have families, and the family lives in the temple, unlike our Chinese monastics and our Chinese temples. Our monastics are recruited from outside; they have no need to recruit — the sons they bear are their own disciples, and their wives live in the temple. That is the kind of Buddhism theirs is. The content of the True School omits all mention of cultivating the three blessings of pure karma, observing precepts, and arousing the bodhi mind.

If you want to arouse the bodhi mind, read and recite the scriptures, observe precepts, cultivate merit, and do good deeds, they consider this miscellaneous practice — just think how they distort the Buddha's teachings!
(One of the marks of the Original Vow school: inverted teaching.)

What do they advocate? Simply reciting the Buddha-name once. Their theory is like this: if we plan to take a train to some place, we need carry nothing at all; one recitation of the Buddha-name is like buying a train ticket, and then we can get there. No matter how much you recite — you can recite while playing mahjong and gambling, you can recite while drinking — you need only recite the Buddha-name once. How distorted this theory is, utterly distorted! Although they advocate Buddha-recitation, in reality it wholly contradicts the Buddha's scriptures and treatises and the Pure Land teaching,
for then evil people may do as much evil as they please: one recitation of the Buddha-name and at death they can be born in the West
(One of the marks of the Original Vow school: inverted teaching)
, and this first point violates the true meaning of our Buddhist principles.
The second point is that it indulges evil people, shielding evil under the name of Buddha-recitation.
Note:

the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Reception, spoken from the golden mouth of our original teacher Śākyamuni Buddha and praised and upheld by Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, says:
“Sentient beings of few roots of goodness shall not be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.
(Translation:
Beings with few roots of goodness cannot be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
In the Buddha Speaks of Amitābha Buddha Sutra, the Buddha says:
“Śāriputra! Not with few roots of goodness, merits, and causes
(not with few causes of roots of goodness and merit)
, can one be born in that land
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
Yet the Original Vow school loudly advocates evil persons as the true recipients. For example, Master Huijing says in The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao:
“One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal Amitābha's Original Vow: evil persons as the true recipients.”
Master Huijing's disciple who took refuge under him, Master Xinyuan, says in Amitābha's Deliverance Takes Evil Persons as the True Recipients:
“Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha's deliverance: what kind of beings does it take as its true recipients? Evil persons are the true recipients.”

[Roots of goodness] are the goodness of the three karmas of body, speech, and mind; because they can produce wondrous fruits they are called roots. [Sentient beings] are also called ‘living beings’, that is, all creatures possessing consciousness.]
Now there are people promoting the Original Vow school, but they meet with opposition everywhere. One of them is named Shengsu (
now renamed Master Jingzong, who went off to take refuge under Master Huijing of Taiwan, who advocates the Original Vow school

). This man has been to Chongqing and also to Lezhi. He first promoted the Original Vow school in Jiangxi; he is from Jiuhua Mountain, and because he promoted this teaching at Jiuhua Mountain, his teacher admonished him, criticized him, and rebuked him; he would not listen, and was driven down the mountain. This time I met his teacher, and the old Dharma master told me: that fellow has wrong views and wrong understanding and spreads nonsense everywhere; I drove him out. Many laypeople do not know about this. After he left he went to Jiangxi and afterwards to Sichuan to spread the Original Vow school; the Jiangxi Religious Affairs Bureau and Public Security Bureau both wanted to make trouble for him, yet he scurried hither and thither and turned up again in Lezhi, Sichuan, and Chongqing,
and what he spreads is a heretical teaching, a crooked path and heretical way

. Laypeople of right faith see this clearly; you must certainly not believe it. Just think: merely recite a phrase of Buddha-recitation, pay no attention to one's way of life — such people do not support their parents and commit killings and offenses far and wide, yet simply by reciting the Buddha-name they are born in the West! What kind of theory is this? The Pure Land scriptures speak of the need for assisting practices, for provisions, for cultivating the three blessings of pure karma — which include human and heavenly goodness, liberating goodness, and bodhisattva goodness — for observing precepts, arousing the bodhi mind, widely planting fields of merit, and widely doing good deeds. How can one who recites the Buddha-name neglect all of this? The Original Vow school does not connect with reality, does not accord with what the Buddha taught, and runs entirely counter to the Humanistic Buddhism advocated by Master Taixu and the Buddhism in the Human Realm advocated by Elder Zhao Puchu.

blocks.text: Appendix 9: Refuting ‘Reciting the Name Brings Certain Birth’ and ‘Evil Persons as the True Recipients’

inline.s: A questioner says: Though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with the power of the vow they are no more than a single grain in the ocean
(though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with Amitābha Buddha's vow-power they are as a single grain of corn beside the great ocean, utterly insignificant)
, and therefore breaking the precepts and doing evil do not matter.
Answer: Amitābha Buddha's vow-power is embodied in the forty-eight great vows. Among them the three vows that gather in beings are:
If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions,
with sincere minds of faith and joy, wishing to be born in my land, recite even ten thoughts
— if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment. Excepted are those who commit the five heinous crimes and slander the true Dharma.
(The Eighteenth Vow)
If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions,
who arouse the bodhi mind, cultivate all merits, and with sincere minds make the vow to be born in my land
— if at the end of their lives I do not appear before them surrounded by a great assembly, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
(The Nineteenth Vow)
If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions who hear my name
fix their thoughts on my land, plant the roots of virtue, and with sincere minds dedicate the merit, wishing to be born in my land
— if their wish is not fulfilled, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
(The Twentieth Vow)

Those who break the precepts and do evil have not ‘cultivated all merits’ or ‘planted the roots of virtue’; on the contrary, they break the precepts and do evil, and so they do not meet the nineteenth and twentieth vows. Do they then meet the eighteenth vow? That depends on whether they can achieve ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death (see
The Eighteenth Vow

for details). Yet can those whose minds are scattered and who indulge themselves in ordinary times arouse right mindfulness when the many sufferings press upon them at death? Can they achieve ten uninterrupted thoughts? If they cannot, and in life they did not observe the precepts but did evil instead, then the destiny their consciousness goes to after death will be determined by the karma of their breaking the precepts and doing evil.
Such cause, such effect — this matters a great deal.

Therefore, to incite people to break the precepts and do evil by the absurd logic that ‘though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with the power of the vow they are no more than a single grain in the ocean, and therefore breaking the precepts and doing evil do not matter’ has extremely serious consequences — it is pushing Buddhist disciples into a pit of fire!

The Original Vow school loudly advocates ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ and ‘evil persons as the true recipients’, and slanderously claims these to be Master Shandao's Pure Land thought. Statements of ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ are everywhere, for example in Master Jingzong's lecture series The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao; so too with ‘evil persons as the true recipients’, for example Master Huijing's statement in The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal Amitābha's Original Vow: evil persons as the true recipients.” And Master Huijing's disciple who took refuge under him, Master Xinyuan, says in Amitābha's Deliverance Takes Evil Persons as the True Recipients: “Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha's deliverance: what kind of beings does it take as its true recipients? Evil persons are the true recipients.”
In the chapter on the lowest grade of the lowest birth in the Buddha Speaks of the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, the World-Honored One teaches:
those who commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evils,
with ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death,
forthwith attain
the extinction of their offenses
and birth in the Pure Land, and their grade is the lowest grade of the lowest birth.
The original text of the sutra reads as follows:

“The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī: As for the lowest grade of the lowest birth, there may be sentient beings who do unwholesome deeds, the five heinous crimes and the ten evils, full of all that is unwholesome. Such foolish people, because of their evil karma, should fall into evil destinies and undergo measureless suffering for many kalpas. When such a foolish person is about to die, he meets a good teacher, who comforts him in various ways and expounds the wondrous Dharma for him, teaching him to recite the Buddha-name. But that person is oppressed by suffering and has no leisure to recite the Buddha-name, so the good friend tells him: ‘If you cannot be mindful of that Buddha, then call upon the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, taking refuge in him.’
Thus with a sincere mind, keeping the sound unbroken, he completes ten thoughts, calling ‘Namo Amitābha Buddha’

. Because he calls the Buddha's name, in each thought he erases the offenses of birth and death of eighty koṭis of kalpas. At the moment of death, he sees a golden lotus flower like the sun's disk appear before him, and in a single thought he is born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Within that lotus flower he remains for twelve great kalpas before the lotus opens. When the flower opens, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, with voices of great compassion, expound for him the Dharma of true reality and the eradication of offenses; hearing it, he rejoices and at once arouses the bodhi mind. This is called the lowest grade of the lowest birth. This is called the contemplation of the lowest grade, the sixteenth contemplation.”
(For annotations, see
Annotations on the Chapter on the Lowest Grade of the Lowest Birth in the Contemplation Sutra
for details)
In his Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra, Master Shandao explains the meaning of this chapter (the chapter on the lowest grade of the lowest birth) as follows:

“From the words ‘such a foolish person’ down to ‘the offenses of birth and death’, this precisely explains how hearing the Dharma and reciting the Buddha-name brings present benefit, and there are ten aspects: first, it restates the evildoer; second, it shows that his life will not last long; third, it shows that at the point of death he meets a good teacher; fourth, it shows the good person comforting him and teaching him to recite the Buddha-name; fifth, it shows that the sinner is pressed by the suffering of death and has no way to be mindful of the Buddha's name; sixth, it shows that the good friend, knowing his suffering and loss of mindfulness, instead teaches him to call aloud Amitābha's name; seventh, it shows how many recitations there are,
each sound uninterrupted
; eighth, it shows the eradication of offenses of many kalpas; ninth, it shows
that with right mindfulness at the time of death, a golden flower comes to receive him
; tenth, it shows the speed of his going, arriving straight at the land to which he returns.”
Please pay special attention to what Master Shandao says in his teaching: “
each sound uninterrupted
” and “
with right mindfulness at the time of death, a golden flower comes to welcome him
”. Combine these with Master Shandao's teachings on ‘continuous recitation brings birth’ and ‘right mindfulness at the time of death’ (see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
for details), and the meaning of these two phrases will become even clearer. And you will clearly know that Master Shandao says in the Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra,
“So long as one can, at the most, do so for a whole lifetime, or at the least, down to ten thoughts, then by the power of the Buddha's vow, none fail to be born; therefore it is called easy,”
and
says in his Liturgy of Birth in the Pure Land,
“If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions who call my name, down to ten utterances — if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment,”
; in these passages, ‘down to ten thoughts’
means ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death

. Yet the Original Vow school distorts it to mean any ten thoughts whatsoever, and then concludes: Master Shandao says reciting the name brings certain birth! (See Master Jingzong's lecture series The Pure Land Thought of Master Shandao.)

Moreover, Master Shandao's statement in the Liturgy of Birth in the Pure Land — ‘If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions who call my name, down to ten utterances, if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment’ — derives from the eighteenth vow in the Buddha Speaks of the Immeasurable Life Sutra

“If I attain Buddhahood, and sentient beings of the ten directions, with sincere minds of faith and joy, wish to be born in my land and recite even ten thoughts — if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment. Excepted are those who commit the five heinous crimes and slander the true Dharma.”
The ‘even ten thoughts’ of the eighteenth vow means
ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death
, as the patriarchs and great teachers of the Pure Land school through the ages have analyzed most clearly (see
The Eighteenth Vow
for details); how could Master Shandao's ‘down to ten thoughts’ mean that reciting the name brings certain birth (that any ten thoughts in ordinary times bring certain birth)?
Moreover, throughout his life Master Shandao upheld
“continuous recitation brings birth”
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching

for details), and Master Yinguang praised this without end: “Its benefit is inexhaustible!” How can one say that Master Shandao upheld ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’? On the contrary, Master Shandao upheld
“continuous recitation brings birth”!
Moreover, as quoted above, Master Shandao states perfectly clearly in the Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra:
With right mindfulness at the time of death
, a golden flower comes to welcome him.”
This means that birth in the Pure Land comes about because of
right mindfulness at the time of death
. How can one say that Master Shandao upheld ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’? On the contrary, Master Shandao upheld
“right mindfulness at the time of death”!
Moreover, in Master Shandao's Text on Right Mindfulness at the Time of Death for Birth in the Pure Land, Master Shandao states with perfect clarity:
only with right mindfulness at the time of death can one be born in the Pure Land
(see
Annotations on Master Shandao's Text on Right Mindfulness at the Time of Death for Birth in the Pure Land
for details). Since right mindfulness at the time of death is required for birth in the Pure Land, how can reciting the name bring certain birth?

Originally, the chapter on the lowest grade of the lowest birth in the Contemplation Sutra teaches that the grade of such a person born in the Pure Land (one who commits the five heinous crimes and the ten evils and yet achieves ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death, erases his offenses, and is born there) is the lowest grade of the lowest birth,
yet the Original Vow school deliberately omits
ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death

, this crucial point, and exaggerates it into the claim that all who commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evils attain birth in the Pure Land, advocating ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ and the so-called ‘doctrine of evil persons as the true recipients’. Master Huijing says in The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal Amitābha's Original Vow: evil persons as the true recipients.” Master Huijing's disciple who took refuge under him, Master Xinyuan, says: “Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha's deliverance: what kind of beings does it take as its true recipients? Evil persons are the true recipients.”

Yet even those who commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evils and attain birth as spoken of in the sutra do so because in past lives they deeply planted roots of goodness and once sowed the seeds of bodhi. Master Ouyi
says
“The sutra says that those who commit the ten evils and five heinous crimes attain birth
because in the past they must have sown the seeds of bodhi

. Without the seeds of bodhi, how could they meet a good friend? And even meeting a good friend who urges and inspires them, how could they at once give rise to faith and vow and call the great name?”
(Lingfeng Zonglun: Shepu Tianma Monastery Universal Teaching)
(Translation

: To accomplish the ten recitations at the time of death, one must deeply plant roots of goodness. If today, the moment adverse or favorable conditions arise, one no longer has right mindfulness, how much less will one be able to keep right mindfulness at the time of death? Moreover, today under clear skies and bright sun, in broad daylight, one still cannot accept and practice the true admonitions of a clear teacher and good friend — and yet one vainly hopes that when the suffering of death appears, one can, merely by relying on a good friend's reminders and instruction, accept and practice them?)
In the Buddha Speaks of Amitābha Buddha Sutra, the Buddha says:
Not with few roots of goodness, merits, and causes
(one cannot do so with few causes of roots of goodness and merit)
, can one be born in that land
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)

[Roots of goodness] are the goodness of the three karmas of body, speech, and mind; because they can produce wondrous fruits they are called roots. [Sentient beings] are also called ‘living beings’, that is, all creatures possessing consciousness.
In the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, the Buddha says:
Those who wish to be born in that land
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
should cultivate the three blessings
: First, to support and serve one's parents, to serve and respect one's teachers, to be compassionate and refrain from killing,
to cultivate the ten wholesome deeds
; second, to receive and uphold the three refuges,
to observe all the precepts
, and not to violate the rules of deportment; third, to arouse the bodhi mind,
to deeply believe in cause and effect
, to read and recite the Mahāyāna scriptures, and to encourage others to practice. These three matters are called pure karma.”
(see
Annotations on the Chapter on the Lowest Grade of the Lowest Birth in the Contemplation Sutra
for details)

Just consider: those disciples and faithful who are bewitched by ‘reciting the name brings certain birth’ and ‘evil persons as the true recipients’ neither recite the Buddha-name with diligence and single-mindedness, nor, believing in ‘evil persons as the true recipients’, end evil and do good, and some even do evil all their lives (including slandering the true Dharma) — do they have the merit and the power to achieve ten uninterrupted thoughts at the time of death? If they cannot, where will they go after death, and what will be the karmic retribution of their future lives, life after life?

blocks.text: Appendix 10: Recognizing the True Face of the So-Called Japanese Shandao-Lineage Original Vow School

inline.s: What is superstition? To lack wisdom and discrimination, to say only what others say, to believe blindly — that is superstition. For example, in our society there is a heterodox path attached to Buddhism (a crooked path and heretical way wearing the outer garment of Buddhism) called the Original Vow school. It has won quite a few followers, and many of us now believe in the Original Vow school. Why do I criticize the Original Vow school? I spent a good deal of time investigating and studying it. First I looked into its history: the origin of the Original Vow school goes back to the time before Liberation, when Japan invaded China. Japan is a country where Buddhism flourished greatly; since the Tang dynasty, when it was transmitted from China — as when Jianzhen crossed eastward — nearly the whole population believed in Buddhism. At that time, when Japan wanted to invade China, its own common people were all Buddhists. If you go to invade another country, you have to kill people — what was to be done? How was this contradiction to be resolved? Buddhists hold that one must not take life. Unlike us — we resisted Japan and killed the Japanese aggressors, but we were acting in self-defense. Japan was the aggressor. So how do you get a Buddhist to take the initiative in invading others? The ancients said that religion sometimes serves politics, and there is deep truth in that saying.

So at that time in Japanese religious circles a situation arose: they advocated blending the Buddha-Dharma into their native Shinto thought, and advocated simplifying Amitābha's Original Vow. So long as you believe — believe in Amitābha Buddha and recite this invocation of Amitābha — you can be born in the Pure Land and attain liberation; it does not matter what you ordinarily do, and all the precepts are thrown away. Later, in the 1930s, the Japanese government sent many fake Buddhists to infiltrate China and carry out preaching and proselytizing, spreading their Original Vow school, with the aim of preparing the way for its troops to enter China: it was fine for you to strive to kill people — although you had killed, so long as you believed in Amitābha Buddha and recited a single ‘Namo Amitābha Buddha’ you could be saved, no problem. This is where it began, because if you want to invade a country and occupy it, you must control its thought; controlling its land is useless, controlling its bodies is useless — you must control its thought. So its aim was to control people's thought. The Original Vow school was spread, first, within its own troops and army, because many in the army were Buddhists. If you did not let them believe in this thing, they would not dare to kill; they were afraid, afraid that killing would bring karmic retribution. That was one aim. Another aim was that the Chinese common people were then in great suffering: they told them, you are suffering — believe in my Original Vow school, just believe and you will be saved, you can be liberated, it is very easy. They came with this aim. In the end, after we won the War of Resistance, we drove the religious forces of the Original Vow school out of our land; they went with Chiang Kai-shek to Taiwan, and later Chiang Kai-shek colluded with them again. Why did he collude with these Japanese? Because he wanted to counterattack the mainland.

He has used the Japanese secret-service organs to train certain personnel in preparation for a counterattack on the mainland; he established a temple of the Primal Vow school in Taiwan, and so the Primal Vow school went to Taiwan and was spread there. Later, when Chiang Kai-shek’s hopes of counterattacking the mainland came to nothing, the Primal Vow school nevertheless gained a certain influence in Taiwan. The Japanese devils’ determination to destroy our China will never cease; their wolfish ambition will never disappear. He therefore transmitted the Primal Vow school through Taiwan to Hong Kong — because directly entering the mainland is impossible; it cannot come straight in — so shifting ground, transmitting it from Hong Kong back to the mainland, slowly spreading it back. First, from the ideological side, washing and brainwashing your mind. Moreover, there is a saying in Japan, reported in many places online: if you but establish on the mainland a temple propagating the Primal Vow school, the Japanese side will contribute ten million yuan. To build your temple, they contribute at least ten million, in covert support. Wherein lies the purpose? To have you build a great temple, expand its influence, occupy the sphere of belief of the common people, and have them accept its ideological indoctrination — this serves that purpose. If a nation loses its own thought and its own culture, that nation is already dead in name but alive in substance. So the Japanese devils, having not won on the battlefield, seek by every means to destroy you — first in religion, in league with the United States. Why cry “freedom of religious belief”? They mean: once I have brought the Primal Vow school in, you cannot touch me. If you touch me, you are obstructing freedom of religious belief. So this is deeply calculated. And it is brandishing the Buddhist
banner

. For Japan’s Shintō (the Way of the Gods) could never be introduced into China. As for his Primal Vow school, the great masters of our mainland have likewise opposed it; he therefore takes a detour through Taiwan and Hong Kong to bring it back in, corrupting you economically, exploiting the current one-sided pursuit of economic development on the part of the Chinese, and cultivating internal contradictions in China in order to disintegrate it. Therein lies his purpose. Slowly, slowly, he comes to control the thinking of our common people.

In Changsha I came into contact with many believers of the Primal Vow school; they recite “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” and whenever they greet anyone it is “Namo Amitabha Buddha.” One of their believers chatted with me. I said “Amitabha Buddha,” and he said “Namo Amitabha Buddha.” When I pronounced “Amitabha Buddha” once, he said, “That won’t do — to recite merely ‘Amitabha Buddha’ is to shed the Buddha’s blood.” He said “Namo Amitabha Buddha” cannot be broken apart; if you leave off the two characters “Namo,” you shed the Buddha’s blood

I said, What is “shedding the Buddha’s blood”? What is the meaning of “Namo”? What is the meaning of “Amitabha Buddha”? He could not answer, because he simply does not understand the meaning of Amitabha Buddha. “Amitabha Buddha” is the complete name of the Buddha’s virtuous qualities; “Namo” means that we take refuge in, revere, and bow to Amitabha Buddha. Therefore when Master Yinguang urged the recitation of the Buddha’s name, it too began with the six characters. Why six characters? Because at that point we had no self-power and lacked self-confidence; so we take refuge in, revere, and bow to Amitabha Buddha, seeking the protective power of his blessing. The purpose lies in this — hence one recites “Namo Amitabha Buddha.” But after one has recited to the end, if faith arises and one still recites “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” then one forever does not believe in oneself, forever believes only in an external Amitabha Buddha, with no Amitabha Buddha within oneself — this is called a heretical path. When we begin to recite, we are ordinary beings weighted by karmic hindrances, so we must rely on Amitabha Buddha — rely on an external Amitabha Buddha — “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” taking refuge in, revering, and bowing to him, so that he blesses us. But once one has recited until the self-Buddha appears, to still recite “Namo” is to forever exclude oneself from Amitabha Buddha, forever incapable of attaining Buddhahood. When you have recited to the end, you no longer need “Namo” — why still take refuge? Because I have already recited the self-Buddha into appearance; I am myself originally Amitabha Buddha. Then one can directly recite the name. So at the beginning, when the power is insufficient, one adds “Namo.” Reciting to the end, if you still must have “Namo,” then you can never enter into the realm of Amitabha Buddha. Every person is Amitabha Buddha — the body of the Dharma-realm, the body of the cosmos, present nowhere and everywhere; we are originally a portion of Amitabha Buddha. Amitabha Buddha is a whole, and we are a portion of the whole. Are we not within Amitabha Buddha? At the beginning, because we cannot recognize ourselves, we add “Namo”; at the end, once we have recognized ourselves, why still seek from without? Amitabha Buddha is right at this present moment. Then the two characters “Namo” can be removed — no longer needed — cutting straight through to the point, directly being Amitabha Buddha. So sometimes I make a joke and say, when you meet a person of that Primal Vow school, one glance tells you he is a heretic. Why? Because when we greet people

it is “Amitabha Buddha.” That means you too are Amitabha Buddha, and I too am Amitabha Buddha. But he, “Namo Amitabha Buddha, Namo Amitabha Buddha,” is always reciting; it means: you are Amitabha Buddha, I must take refuge in, revere, and bow to you — and so he himself is not Amitabha Buddha. He can forever never be the same as Amitabha Buddha — is this not seeking the Dharma outside the mind? If one always recites “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” one forever does not believe that one can attain Buddhahood, forever outside Amitabha Buddha. That is precisely why it is called an external (heretical) path — and so it is a heretical path attached to Buddhism.

The above is an analysis of it in theory. In fact, having been paying attention to it in this period, I deliberately looked at their “Primal Vow Mountain” in Anhui. The books written by the masters on the mountain are riddled with holes in their theory. For example, they dare not acknowledge the successive patriarchs; they only drag out Master Shandao of the Tang dynasty, yet the Primal Vow taught by Master Shandao and their “Primal Vow” are entirely mismatched — they merely borrowed the name of Master Shandao. Then why does it gain so many followers? Because sentient beings are superstitious
unable to tell the true from the false, helpless
What he teaches is a counterfeit Dharma; he brandishes the Buddhist
banner

, dragging out Master Shandao. How many of the ordinary public have ever read Master Shandao’s writings? They have not; you do not know what Master Shandao actually said. So whatever Primal Vow Mountain says is taken as it stands. One only knows that Master Shandao is a reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha, and that what he said cannot be wrong. The ordinary public all have this mentality; where would they have the ability and the energy to understand the Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sūtra that Master Shandao wrote? Not having read it, they say it is so — they say Master Shandao said exactly this — and you think it is right, and they drag you along with them. And there is another point: Anhui Primal Vow Mountain built a very large temple, with local support, because they have money. And where does the money come from — Hong Kong and Taiwan. Is it really Hong Kong and Taiwan? That is why I want to trace out this cause; I want to trace it back to Japan — their money comes from Japan, laundered through Taiwan and Hong Kong. Including the Zizhulin in Gaogiao town, Changsha County, near us — within a few years it flourished enormously and even received commendations from the relevant quarters. Why? Because it has money! Whoever has money has ability. They do not care whether you are orthodox or heretical; they only look at the money. The Purple Bamboo Mountain built up a great size within a few years; where did its funds come from? It says they came over from Taiwan and Hong Kong — “From Japan!” I tell you.

So we, as Chinese people, if we lack even this vigilance, then in the end something will go wrong and we will not know how it happened. Do not believe their devilish talk, I tell you! The Primal Vow school by no means has any genuine good will toward us — that is absolutely impossible, I tell you! Because the general public has not studied it,
Japan’s

culture is itself a wolfish culture bearing the character of aggression; only our Chinese culture is the true culture of harmony. To imagine it will be harmonious with you is impossible. Only when we are stronger than it can we truly achieve harmony — and we will not aggress against others. Moreover, regarding this Master Jingzong himself: he is fundamentally a false monk who, in collusion with the imported Japanese Primal Vow school, was expelled from the gate of Mount Jiuhua by his own teacher, the Great Master Rende — the monk Shi Shengsu

His — that Anhui Hongyuan Temple, deliberately Japanese in style — deceives ignorant believers, propagates wrong views, and has fabricated many groundless, unreliable cases of rebirth. The whole temple has no public account. It is precisely from this point that I investigated him: a temple as large as it is, yet there is no public account — only a personal account of his own, and several bank accounts are all personal. When Shi Jingzong wants others to send money, it goes directly into his personal account. With a temple this large and such great capital flows, how can one open the accounts in a personal name? This is simply not in accord with the Dharma.

With a personal account, you alone can take as you please; there is no one to supervise you. One person is private; three persons make it public. So if you build such a great temple — as a Dharma-propagating place where one preaches the Dharma — do you not know even the basic national financial system? At the very least, a temple as large as the Hongyuan Temple should open an account in the name of the Hongyuan Temple — a public account — so that mutual supervision is exercised; this is the most basic thing. So on this very point as well, he is not in accord with the Dharma.

Not to mention that his funds are Japanese-supported, and that what he propagates is an extreme other-power domination, the thought of the Shintō way of the gods, a typical heretical path attached to Buddhism. On the one hand, they aim to destroy the Buddha-Dharma, abolishing the precepts as teacher; on the other, they prepare ideologically for a future alliance of the United States and Japan to bring down Chinese culture. Therein lies their purpose. Let us never believe that they have any good intent; to understand a bit of Japanese culture is to make it clear: Japanese culture is a kind of transformed, servile culture, and it is deeply inferior! Why is it inferior? Because it has no culture of its own; it was influenced from childhood by our China and cannot shake off China’s shadow. In the Meiji era of modern times, why did it so avidly study the West? It wanted to throw off China. Because the roots of its culture come from China, from our Confucianism and Buddhism — all transmitted over from us. Its nation has a sense of inferiority; the whole Japanese nation has a sense of inferiority. It always wants to emphasize that it is stronger than others. Yet it cannot shake off China’s influence, and so it studies the West — but in its bones the roots still come from China, and learning the West it cannot imitate it aright, and so a distorted mentality arises. Yet it dares not acknowledge it; having erred, it dares not acknowledge it. It aggressed against China, yet to its death it is unwilling to acknowledge it. Of such a country, can you hold good thoughts? Japan holds no good impression in my book. So that Primal Vow school, transmitted by them and heavily tinged with politics, is something that we as Buddhists must resolutely oppose; we must see clearly its essence and not be led by the nose. May it not come to the point of a knife at your neck, and you still die confused and utterly willing. As Buddhists, we must understand this clearly.

In our present society, some people put money above all; they care not what Dharma-gate it is, only about present profit. But ultimately what heretical doctrines corrupt is our Buddhism — they destroy our Buddhism. So in this present situation, when we Buddhists stand up and oppose the Primal Vow school, some may say that is an internal matter of Buddhism — that we Buddhists are internally disharmonious.

This is not a matter of internal disharmony. I earnestly remind everyone: it bears on the question of cultural aggression, on severing the roots of your culture — this is not a small matter. This so-called Japanese Shandao-lineage Primal Vow heretical doctrine, propagated chiefly by the abbot of the Anhui Japanese-based Hongyuan Temple (the monk Shengsu, that is, Master Jingzong, publicly expelled from the Buddhist order by the Great Master Rende, the head abbot of the whole of Mount Jiuhua) and by the Taiwanese Master Huijing, who once studied in Japan, has entered China and is propagandizing on a grand scale, turning Amitabha Buddha into a god, an externalized deity, a God, with the further aim of abolishing the Buddhist precepts and denying and rejecting the three studies of precepts, meditation, and wisdom —
in order to
